docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:48:When multiple sessions are ACTIVE in the same directory and one session's agent (or subagent) makes a commit, **all** ACTIVE sessions are condensed — including sessions that didn't contribute to the commit. This can produce checkpoint entries with minimal content (e.g., just the initial prompt) linked to a commit the session didn't work on.
docs/KNOWN_LIMITATIONS.md:50:**Why:** PostCommit sets `hasNew=true` for all ACTIVE sessions. We cannot re-validate via transcript analysis because subagent file modifications live in a separate transcript from the main agent's. Attempting to re-validate causes subagent commits to skip condensation entirely (data loss), which is worse than a spurious empty checkpoint.
docs/security-and-privacy.md:11:Entire also creates temporary local branches (e.g., `entire/<short-hash>`) as working storage during a session. Metadata written to these shadow branches — transcripts, prompts, incremental checkpoint data, subagent transcripts — goes through the same redaction pipeline as `entire/checkpoints/v1`. **Code-file snapshots, however, are written as raw blobs of your working tree without redaction**, so any hardcoded secrets in your source code would appear unredacted on the shadow branch. Gitignored files (e.g., `.env`) are filtered out of these snapshots as a partial defense. Shadow branches are **not** pushed by Entire; do not push them manually, because unredacted source content would be visible on the remote. They are cleaned up when session data is condensed into `entire/checkpoints/v1` at commit time.

128	### Strategy-Level Operations
129	
130	Strategies compose low-level primitives into higher-level workflows.
131	
132	**Manual-commit** has condensation logic:
133	
134	```go
135	// CondenseSession reads accumulated temporary state and writes a committed checkpoint.
136	func (s *ManualCommitStrategy) CondenseSession(
137	    repo *git.Repository,
138	    checkpointID id.CheckpointID,
139	    state *SessionState,

142	
143	## Storage
144	
145	| Type | Location | Contents |
146	|------|----------|----------|
147	| Session State | `.git/entire-sessions/<id>.json` | Active session tracking |
148	| Ephemeral | `entire/<commit[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>` branch | Full state (code + metadata) |
149	| Persistent (git-branch) | `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch, sharded `<id[:2]>/<id[2:]>/` | Metadata + commit reference |
150	| Persistent (git-refs) | `refs/entire/checkpoints/<shard>/<id>`, one ref per checkpoint | Metadata + commit reference |
151	
152	The persistent store is pluggable: `git-branch` stores every committed checkpoint as a subtree of a single `entire/checkpoints/v1` branch, while `git-refs` stores one ref per checkpoint. New setups write an explicit backend choice via `entire enable` (`git-refs` recommended and pre-selected); a repo with no checkpoints config still resolves to `git-branch` (the config-less fallback), so pre-existing repos keep their behavior. Both are git-backed and share the same checkpoint tree layout; they differ only in where that tree is committed. This document describes the git-branch layout; for the ref-based backend — its ref naming, sharding, push/fetch model, read routing, and configuration — see [Ref-Based Checkpoint Backend](ref-checkpoint-backend.md).
153	
154	### Session State
155	
156	Location: `.git/entire-sessions/<session-id>.json`
157	
158	Stored in git common dir (shared across worktrees). Tracks active session info.
159	
160	The state records `Branch` — the branch HEAD pointed at on the session's last turn
161	(captured each turn start, so it follows branches created/renamed after the
162	session began). `entire resume` (bare, no arg) uses it to list stopped sessions
163	and map each back to its branch; for sessions recorded before the field existed
164	it falls back to deriving the branch from the session's last checkpoint ID found
165	in branch-only commit trailers.
166	
167	`entire session adopt` moves an active session from a source repo or worktree
168	into the current worktree. Adoption preserves the live transcript path, validates
169	that the source state still belongs to the requested source worktree, rewrites
170	the session's branch/worktree/base metadata to the target, clears target-local
171	checkpoint windows and checkpoint IDs, and snapshots the target's current file
172	changes so the next commit can link to the adopted session.
173	
174	### Temporary Checkpoints
175	
176	Branch: `entire/<commit[:7]>-<worktreeHash[:6]>`
177	
178	Contains full worktree snapshot plus metadata overlay. **Multiple concurrent sessions** can share the same shadow branch - their checkpoints interleave:
179	
180	```
181	<worktree files...>
182	.entire/metadata/<session-id-1>/
183	├── full.jsonl           # Session 1 transcript
184	├── prompt.txt           # Checkpoint-scoped user prompts
185	└── tasks/<tool-use-id>/ # Task checkpoints
186	.entire/metadata/<session-id-2>/
187	├── full.jsonl           # Session 2 transcript (concurrent)
188	├── ...
189	```
190	
191	Tied to a base commit. Condensed to committed on user commit.
192	
193	**Transcript sanitization (before redaction).** Entire never modifies the agent's
194	own transcript, but the copy it stores goes through the agent's optional
195	`agent.TranscriptSanitizer` first, at the point Entire takes custody (the Stop path
196	in `lifecycle.go`, before `.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl` is written). Codex
197	implements it to strip encrypted reasoning payloads and compaction blobs, which are
198	bound to the originating session and cannot be replayed out of a checkpoint.
199	
200	Sanitization always runs before redaction, but the paths differ in whether image
201	externalization happens at all:
202	
203	| Path | Pipeline | Where |
204	|---|---|---|
205	| Stop (shadow branch) | sanitize → redact | `lifecycle.go` sanitizes before `full.jsonl` is written; the metadata-dir walker (`createRedactedBlobFromFile`) redacts it into the shadow tree |
206	| Post-commit condensation | sanitize → externalize → redact | `prepareTranscriptForStorage` in `manual_commit_condensation.go` |
207	| Stop finalize (full-session rewrite) | sanitize → externalize → redact | `manual_commit_hooks.go`, before `extractSessionImages` |
208	
209	**Image externalization runs only on the committed paths** (condensation and
210	finalize). The shadow-branch copy is never externalized, so inline images there are
211	subject to redaction like any other high-entropy content — do not assume a shadow
212	transcript preserves them. Assets and the `assets/manifest.json` index exist only
213	under committed checkpoints.
214	
215	Where all three steps run, each must precede the next. Sanitizing first avoids
216	externalizing images out of items that are about to be discarded — that would store
217	an asset whose referencing transcript line disappears moments later — and avoids
218	redacting megabytes of ciphertext only to throw it away; base64 is the pathological
219	input for the entropy layer, so a large Codex rollout otherwise costs tens of seconds
220	per Stop *and* per commit. Externalizing before redaction is required because base64
221	is high-entropy and redaction would otherwise flag and destroy it.
222	
223	The sanitize transform is idempotent, so a downstream write path can call it without
224	knowing whether an upstream path already did (`checkpoint.sanitizeForAgentType` is
225	the store's own belt-and-braces call).
226	
227	One coupling to respect when changing this: `SessionState.CheckpointTranscriptSize`
228	is a growth baseline compared against the shadow transcript blob's size in
229	`sessionHasNewContent`, so it must be measured in the same (sanitized) coordinate —
230	see `CondenseResult.TranscriptSizeBaseline`. A raw baseline against a sanitized blob
231	makes the comparison false forever and the session silently stops condensing.
232	
233	**Shadow branch lifecycle:**
234	- Created on first checkpoint for a base commit
235	- Migrated automatically if base commit changes (stash → pull → apply scenario)
236	- Deleted after condensation to `entire/checkpoints/v1`
237	- Reset if orphaned (no session state file exists)

239	### Committed Checkpoints
240	
241	Branch: `entire/checkpoints/v1`
242	
243	Committed checkpoints sync to exactly one git remote — the elected checkpoint
244	sync remote, resolved in this order:
245	
246	1. `strategy_options.checkpoint_push_remote` if set — fail-closed when it
247	   names a remote that is not configured (checkpoint sync is disabled until
248	   fixed, since this is explicit user intent).
249	2. `origin`, if configured.
250	3. The sole configured remote.
251	4. The first remote in `.git/config` order.
252	
253	The branch's tracking config (`branch.<name>.pushRemote`,
254	`remote.pushDefault`, `branch.<name>.remote`) is deliberately **not** a tier.
255	Election is compared against the remote of the push being made, so electing
256	the tracking remote turns every push to a different remote into a silent
257	no-op — `git push <other> HEAD`, a `git clone -o base` whose checkpoints go to
258	a separately added `origin`, any repo with `remote.pushDefault` set. It would
259	also elect a remote the read paths cannot see, since `resume` and `explain`
260	resolve checkpoints through origin's remote-tracking refs.
261	
262	For the fork setup where `origin` is an unpushable base repo, name the fork
263	explicitly with `checkpoint_push_remote` — the only form of it where the
264	checkpoints can also be read back.

267	elected remote; pushes to any other remote or to a raw URL sync nothing, on
268	both the git-branch and git-refs backends (git-refs leaves its push queue
269	intact for the next elected-remote push). The dedicated `checkpoint_remote`
270	URL mode is exempt — it addresses a separate metadata store directly. `entire
271	status` shows the sync destination and how many checkpoints have not reached

- Use read-modify-write on entire `hooks.json` file
- Preserve unknown keys in the `hooks` object (future event types)
- The `hooks.json` is separate from `config.toml` — safe to create/modify independently

## CLI Flags

- Non-interactive prompt: `codex exec "<prompt>"` or `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox "<prompt>"`
- Interactive mode: `codex` or `codex "<prompt>"` (starts TUI)
- Resume session: `codex resume <session-id>` or `codex resume --last`
- Model override: `-m <model>` or `--model <model>`
- Full-auto mode: `codex exec --full-auto "<prompt>"` (workspace-write sandbox + auto-approve)
- JSONL output: `codex exec --json "<prompt>"` (events to stdout)
- Relevant env vars: `CODEX_HOME` (config dir override), `OPENAI_API_KEY` (API auth)

## Gaps & Limitations

- **Hooks require feature flag:** The `codex_hooks` feature is `default_enabled: false` (stage: UnderDevelopment). It must be enabled via `--enable codex_hooks` CLI flag, or `features.codex_hooks = true` in `config.toml`, or `-c features.codex_hooks=true`. Without this, hooks.json is ignored entirely.
- **No SessionEnd hook:** Codex does not fire a hook when a session is completely terminated. The `Stop` hook fires at end-of-turn, not end-of-session. This is similar to some other agents — the framework handles this gracefully.
- **PreToolUse is shell-only:** Currently only fires for `Bash` tool (direct shell execution). MCP tools, stdin streaming, and other tool types are not yet hooked. PostToolUse is in review.
- **Transcript may be null:** In `--ephemeral` mode, `transcript_path` is null. The integration should handle this gracefully.
- **No subagent hooks:** No PreTask/PostTask equivalent for subagent spawning.
- **Hook response protocol differs from Claude Code:** Codex uses `systemMessage` (same field name) but also supports `hookSpecificOutput` with `additionalContext` for injecting context into the model. For Entire's purposes, `systemMessage` is sufficient.

## Captured Payloads

- JSON schemas at `codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/` in the Codex repository
- Hook config structure at `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/config.rs` in the Codex repository

## Review integration (`entire review`)

Codex review runs via `codex exec --skip-git-repo-check --json [-m <model>] [-c model_reasoning_effort=<level>] -` (prompt on stdin). **`codex exec` fires no lifecycle hooks**, which shapes the whole integration (see CLAUDE.md → `entire review` → "Codex specifics"):

- **Skills are passed verbatim, not paraphrased.** Codex injects its installed-skill catalog into every exec session and loads the matching `SKILL.md`; configured skills use codex's `$name` / `$plugin:name` form (`DiscoverReviewSkills` in `discovery.go`). Native `codex exec review` is not used — it rejects a prompt under a scope flag and can't carry Entire's scope/per-run/checkpoint context.
- **Live tokens come from the rollout file, not stdout.** `codex exec --json` carries `usage` only on the terminal `turn.completed`, and a review is a single turn. `review_tokens.go` resolves the rollout transcript by `thread_id` (from the `thread.started` envelope), tails it (the same `~/.codex/.../rollout-*-<thread-id>.jsonl` documented under Transcript above), and emits cumulative `Tokens` per `token_count` event — the source codex's interactive UI reads.
- **No tagged review session.** Because no hook fires, codex's session is never tagged `KindAgentReview`. The fix manifest therefore sources codex from its **live run output** (`run.Buffer`), and `entire review fix` skill verification is advisory for codex (loose description match), not a hard block.

name: subagent-tracking-gaps
description: Verified state of subagent tracking in the CLI (2026-08-10) — CC transcript-path bug, no subagent data in committed checkpoints, codex now has subagent hooks, pi subagents hijack the parent session
metadata:
  type: project
---

Investigated 2026-08-10 with hook-level probes against the real binary plus upstream
sources at `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/codex` and `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/pi-mono`.

**Claude Code (2.1.221) subagent transcript path is wrong.** `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd`
resolves `AgentTranscriptPath(filepath.Dir(SessionRef), agentID)` → `<slug>/agent-<id>.jsonl`,
but CC now stores it at `<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` (plus a
`agent-<id>.meta.json` carrying `agentType`, `description`, `toolUseId`, `spawnDepth`).
So `SubagentTranscriptPath` is always empty in production — confirmed: every real
`"subagent completed"` log line across three repos lacks the `subagent_transcript` attr,
and shadow `tasks/<id>/` holds only `checkpoint.json`, no subagent transcript. The TurnEnd
extractor (`lifecycle.go` ~line 848) uses the *correct* `<dir>/<sessionID>/subagents` path,
which masks the bug because files get picked up at Stop.

**Committed checkpoints carry zero subagent data.** Condensation (`extractSessionData`)
reads only `full.jsonl` + `prompt.txt` from the shadow tree, so `tasks/<tool-use-id>/`
is dropped. 0 of 80 primary checkpoint refs in the `cli` repo contain `tasks/`; only a
legacy `v2/full` bundle does. `subagent_tokens` is null in every sampled committed
checkpoint (the two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` in
`manual_commit_condensation.go` are why). `TaskStepContext` has no `TokenUsage` field at
all, and the persistent store's `IsTask`/`tasks/` write path is never invoked in production.

**Codex 0.147 DOES have subagent hooks now** — `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop` schemas in
`codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/`; stop payload includes `agent_id`, `agent_type`,
`agent_transcript_path`, `turn_id`. `hooks` and `multi_agent` are both `stable/true`.
`cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/AGENT.md` claiming "No subagent hooks" and "hooks require
feature flag" is stale.

**Pi subagents hijack the parent session.** Pi has no subagent events; subagents come from
the `subagent/` example extension, which spawns `pi --mode json -p --no-session` with
`cwd` = project dir. That child auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts`
and fires Entire's hooks. With `--no-session` there is no `session_file`, so pi's
`readCachedSessionID` (a single per-repo file, not per-process) returns the *parent's* ID.
Probed effect: child `session_start` errors "no session_id"; child `before_agent_start`
succeeds and overwrites the parent's `last_prompt` with the subagent's internal task text
and starts a new `turn_id`; child `agent_end` fails "transcript file not specified".

**Test coverage gaps:** the Vogon/roger-roger canary fires no subagent hooks at all
(`e2e/vogon/main.go` has no pre-task/post-task), so `TestSubagentCommitFlow` passes without
exercising the path; the real-agent version asserts nothing subagent-specific. Only
`cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/subagent_*.go` covers it, via simulated hooks against the
old transcript layout. `docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md` says nothing
about subagents.

Local run constraints: `mise run test:e2e --agent claude-code` can't authenticate outside CI
(`cleanConfigDir` gives a blank `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; CI links `~/.claude/.claude.json`).
Hook-level probing needs `entire` on PATH or git hooks silently no-op.

content.text:
## What I tested

Real-agent E2E didn't work out here, so I probed the production hook entrypoints directly (temp repos, real `entire` binary, real upstream payload shapes) and cross-checked against your own production logs and checkpoints.

| Probe | Result |
|---|---|
| Vogon canary `TestSubagentCommitFlow` | Passes — but **fires no subagent hooks at all**; `e2e/vogon/main.go` has no pre-task/post-task. Zero real coverage. |
| Claude Code real E2E | **Blocked locally**: `cleanConfigDir` hands the agent a blank `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`, so it reports "Not logged in". Only works in CI (which links `~/.claude/.claude.json`). |
| Claude Code hook-level probe | pre-task → post-task → stop → commit all fire correctly; task checkpoint lands on the shadow branch and shows as `[Task] Completed 'dev' agent: …` in `checkpoint list`. |
| Codex real E2E | You declined the run — not executed. |
| Codex hooks | No subagent verbs registered (`session-start`, `user-prompt-submit`, `stop`, `pre-tool-use`, `post-tool-use` only). |
| Pi nested-subagent probe | Parent session gets hijacked (details below). |

## Four confirmed defects

**1. Claude Code's subagent transcript is never captured.** `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` (`cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1152`) looks for `<slug>/agent-<id>.jsonl`. CC 2.1.221 actually writes `<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`. Production proof: every `"subagent completed"` line in `cli/`, `cli_experiments/` and `cli_experiments_2/` logs has `agent_id` but no `subagent_transcript` attr — it only logs when the path resolves. Consequence: task checkpoints store no subagent transcript, and file extraction silently falls back to scanning the *main* transcript, where the subagent's edits don't appear. The TurnEnd extractor at `lifecycle.go:848` uses the correct path, which is why files still get picked up at Stop — that masks it.

Bonus: upstream now also writes `agent-<id>.meta.json` with `agentType`, `description`, `toolUseId`, `spawnDepth` — ready-made attribution, including nesting depth, which Entire doesn't model.

**2. Committed checkpoints carry no subagent data.** `extractSessionData` reads only `full.jsonl` + `prompt.txt` from the shadow tree, so `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` is dropped at condensation. **0 of 80** primary checkpoint refs in your `cli` repo contain `tasks/` (the 69 hits I found are in a legacy `v2/full` bundle). `subagent_tokens` is `null` in all 30 checkpoints I sampled — including sessions that ran dozens of subagents. The two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` in `manual_commit_condensation.go` are exactly this. `TaskStepContext` has no `TokenUsage` field, and the persistent store's `IsTask`/`tasks/` layout is never written in production.

**3. Codex has subagent hooks now and we ignore them.** `codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/` defines `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop`; the stop payload carries `agent_id`, `agent_type`, **`agent_transcript_path`**, `turn_id`. Both `hooks` and `multi_agent` are `stable/true` in 0.147. `codex/AGENT.md` still says "No subagent hooks" and "hooks require feature flag" — both stale.

**4. Pi subagents corrupt the parent session.** Pi has no subagent events; subagents come from the `subagent/` example extension, which spawns `pi --mode json -p --no-session` with `cwd` = the project. That child auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts` and fires our hooks. With no session file, pi's `readCachedSessionID` — one per-repo file, not per-process — returns the *parent's* ID. Probed: child `session_start` errors `no session_id`; child `before_agent_start` **succeeds and overwrites the parent's `last_prompt`** with the subagent's internal `Task: …` text and starts a fresh `turn_id`; child `agent_end` fails `transcript file not specified`. So the checkpoint title becomes the last subagent's internal prompt and turn windows reset mid-turn.

## What needs doing

**Fix the bugs (small, high value)**
1. Resolve the CC subagent transcript at `<dir>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl`, keeping the old path as fallback. Read `meta.json` for `agentType`/`description`/`spawnDepth` instead of only parsing `tool_input`.
2. Guard pi against nested invocations (mark the child via env when spawning is detectable, or refuse a turn whose session ID came from cache with no session file) so it can't clobber the parent's prompt/turn.
3. Pass the subagents dir at the two condensation TODOs, or explicitly document why not — right now `subagent_tokens` never survives a commit.

**Decide the data model (the actual "proper tracking" question)**
4. Should subagent work be visible *after* commit? If yes: carry `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` into the committed tree (the persistent store already has the layout), enrich the task record — today it's just `session_id`/`tool_use_id`/`checkpoint_uuid`/`agent_id`, with no subagent type, description, files, tokens, or timings — and surface it (`explain`, `status`, `session tokens` already has a Subagents row it can rarely populate). If no, say so in the docs and stop building toward it.
5. Replace the cumulative-`SubagentTokens`-with-delta-rescoping-in-three-places contract with a per-subagent record; it's the fragile core of the token story.

**Codex + Pi integration**
6. Wire codex `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop` → `SubagentStart`/`SubagentEnd` (its `agent_transcript_path` makes this the cleanest integration of the three), plus a `SubagentAwareExtractor` over subagent rollouts. Refresh `AGENT.md`.
7. For pi, decide whether extension-provided subagents are in scope at all; if yes it needs a `tool_call`-based bridge in `entire_extension.ts`, since there's no native event.

**Coverage**
8. Teach Vogon to fire pre-task/post-task so the canary actually exercises the path in CI.
9. Make `TestSubagentCommitFlow` assert something subagent-specific (task checkpoint exists, subagent transcript stored, subagent tokens non-nil).
10. Add a subagent section to `docs/architecture/agent-integration-checklist.md` — it currently says nothing, so every new agent integration skips this.

Probe repos are kept under `…/scratchpad/probe-cc`, `probe-cc2`, `probe-pi` if you want to replay any of it. Want me to run the Codex E2E (it was declined) or start on the two path bugs?

Fires after a subagent finishes its work. Creates the final checkpoint for the subagent's task.

**What it does:**

1.  **Parse Input**: Extracts `tool_use_id`, `agent_id` (from `tool_response.agentId`), `session_id`, `transcript_path`, and `tool_input`.

2.  **Locate Subagent Transcript**:

    - Constructs path: `<transcript_dir>/agent-<agent_id>.jsonl`.
    - If the subagent transcript exists, uses it for file extraction; otherwise falls back to main transcript.

3.  **Extract Modified Files**: Parses the transcript (subagent or main) to find Write/Edit tool invocations.

4.  **Compute New Files**:

    - Loads pre-task state from `.entire/tmp/pre-task-<tool-use-id>.json`.
    - Compares current untracked files against the pre-task snapshot.
    - Files that are now untracked but weren't before = files created by the subagent.

5.  **Find Checkpoint UUID**: Scans the main transcript for any checkpoint UUID associated with this `tool_use_id` (used for rewind linking).

6.  **Save Final Checkpoint**:

    - Builds `TaskCheckpointContext` with all file changes, transcript paths, subagent info, and checkpoint UUID.
    - Calls `strategy.SaveTaskCheckpoint(ctx)`.
    - Creates a commit with the subagent's file changes and metadata including the subagent transcript.

7.  **Cleanup**: Deletes `.entire/tmp/pre-task-<tool-use-id>.json`.

### `PostToolUse[TaskCreate|TaskUpdate]`

- **Command**: `entire hooks claude-code post-todo`
=== line 120-130 ===

5.  **Calculate Token Usage**:

    - Parses the transcript from `StepTranscriptStart` (captured at prompt start) to calculate tokens used in this turn.
    - Extracts token counts from assistant messages: input tokens, cache creation/read tokens, output tokens.
    - Deduplicates by message ID (streaming creates multiple rows per message; uses highest output_tokens).
    - Finds spawned subagents by scanning for `agentId:` in Task tool results.
    - Calculates subagent token usage from their transcript files (`agent-<id>.jsonl`).
    - Aggregates into a `TokenUsage` struct with nested `SubagentTokens`.

6.  **Invoke Strategy**:

    - Builds a `SaveContext` with session ID, file lists, metadata paths, git author info, and token usage.

git push -q -u origin soph/fix-subagent-transcript-path 2>&1 | tail -3 && gh pr create --title "fix(subagent): resolve subagent transcripts in Claude Code's current layout" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` resolved the subagent transcript as a **sibling** of the main transcript:

```
<transcriptDir>/agent-<agentID>.jsonl
```

Claude Code (verified on 2.1.221) nests them one level deeper:

```
<transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<agentID>.jsonl
<transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<agentID>.meta.json   # agentType, description, toolUseId, spawnDepth
```

So the resolved path never existed and `SubagentTranscriptPath` was always empty in production. Evidence: across three enabled repos, **every** real `"subagent completed"` log line carries `agent_id` but never the `subagent_transcript` attribute — that attribute is only appended when the path resolves.

Two consequences:

1. Task checkpoints stored **no subagent transcript** — the shadow tree's `tasks/<tool-use-id>/` held only `checkpoint.json`.
2. File extraction fell back to scanning the **main** transcript from offset 0, where a subagent's `Write`/`Edit` calls never appear.

The turn-end extractor (`lifecycle.go`) already used the correct nested path, so a subagent's files were still picked up at Stop. That masked the bug.

## Fix

- `ResolveAgentTranscriptPath(transcriptDir, sessionID, agentID)` — prefers the nested layout, falls back to the legacy sibling layout so sessions from older agent versions keep working, returns `""` when neither exists (and never resolves an empty `agentID`).
- `SubagentsDir(transcriptDir, sessionID)` — one definition of the nested directory; the turn-end extractor now uses it too instead of inlining the join.

Scoped to path resolution. The `meta.json` sidecar is documented but not yet consumed — richer subagent attribution is separate follow-up work.

## Tests

- `TestResolveAgentTranscriptPath` — nested, legacy, nested-wins-over-legacy, neither-exists, empty-agent-ID.
- `TestSubagentCheckpoints_StoresSubagentTranscript_CurrentLayout` (integration) — asserts the shadow branch contains `tasks/<tool-use-id>/agent-<id>.jsonl` and that it references the subagent's edit. **Verified RED before the fix**, green after.
- `TestSubagentCheckpoints_StoresSubagentTranscript_LegacyLayout` (integration) — regression guard for the old layout.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" 2>&1 | tail -3

### Plugin File Pattern (Pi)

Pi uses a TypeScript extension file (`.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts`) instead of a JSON config. The extension is embedded in the Go binary via `//go:embed` and installed by `entire enable --agent pi`.

Pi extension hooks fire via `execFile` (non-blocking) to avoid blocking the agent. The extension listens for Pi lifecycle events (`session_start`, `before_agent_start`, `agent_end`, `session_shutdown`) and dispatches each to `entire hooks pi <event>` with a JSON payload containing `type`, `cwd`, `session_file`, `session_id`, and (for `before_agent_start`) `prompt`.

Key differences from JSON config agents:
- Extension file is written/removed entirely (not partial JSON edits)
- Uses `node:child_process.execFile` for all hook invocations
- Session ID is cached to `.entire/tmp/pi/pi-active-session` to bridge races between `session_start` and `before_agent_start`/`agent_end`
- On `agent_end`, the Pi JSONL transcript is captured to `.entire/tmp/pi/<id>.json` for stable reference even if native Pi sessions are deleted
- `session_shutdown` is cleanup-only (no `SessionEnd` event) to avoid a race with `agent_end`'s checkpoint save
- Idempotency via marker string check: `"Auto-generated by \`entire enable --agent pi\`"`

See `cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/entire_extension.ts` for the full extension source.

### Plugin File Pattern (OpenCode)

OpenCode uses a TypeScript plugin file (`.opencode/plugins/entire.ts`) instead of a JSON config. The plugin is auto-generated by `entire enable --agent opencode` and uses OpenCode's Bun-based plugin API.

git push -q -u origin soph/fix-pi-nested-subagent-session 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --title "fix(pi): stop nested subagent processes from claiming the parent session" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Pi has no subagent lifecycle events. Subagents come from an extension — see Pi's `subagent/` example — which spawns one nested process per task:

```
pi --mode json -p --no-session      # cwd = the project directory
```

Pi auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/*/index.ts` from that cwd, so **the child loads Entire's own extension** and forwards its lifecycle as if it were the user's session. Because it runs with `--no-session` it reports no session file, so the payload carries no resolvable session ID — and the session-ID cache is a single per-repo file, so the unconditional fallback handed the child its **parent's** ID.

Probed against the real hook entrypoints:

| Child hook | Before |
| --- | --- |
| `session_start` | errors `no session_id in SessionStart event` |
| `before_agent_start` | **succeeds** — overwrites the parent's `last_prompt` with the subagent's internal `Task: …` text and opens a new `turn_id` mid-flight |
| `agent_end` | fails `transcript file not specified` |

So the checkpoint's title and its turn-scoped transcript/token windows described the subagent instead of the user's request.

## Fix

Two guards, so neither has to be perfect:

1. **Extension** — returns early when `process.env.ENTIRE_PI_NESTED` is already set, and sets it otherwise so any Pi this process spawns is marked nested. The marker is read **only** by the extension: Entire's own hook subprocesses inherit it, so the CLI side must never treat it as a skip signal.
2. **CLI** (`nestedInvocation`) — refuses to resolve a payload with no session file against the cache. This also covers third-party subagent extensions and Pi builds that predate the marker.

Preserved:

- The legitimate cache fallback — session file present, but its name carries no parseable ID.
- An explicit payload `session_id`; only the *cache* is distrusted.
- `agent_end` loses nothing: `captureTranscript` returns `""` without a session file, so such an event could only ever fail downstream with "transcript file not specified". The guard turns that error into a clean skip.

## Tests

- `TestParseHookEvent_NestedInvocation_DoesNotClaimParentSession` — a populated parent cache, then the three child payloads with no session file: no event emitted, parent's cache untouched. **Verified RED** (`nested before_agent_start emitted TurnStart for session "parent-id"`).
- `TestParseHookEvent_CacheFallbackStillAppliesWithSessionFile` — regression guard for the legitimate fallback.
- `TestParseHookEvent_ExplicitSessionIDNeedsNoSessionFile` — explicit IDs still honoured.
- `TestInstallHooks` now asserts the installed extension carries the nesting guard.

Also verified end to end against the real binary: after the nested lifecycle, the parent session's `last_prompt` and `turn_id` are unchanged and no second session appears.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

import (

	"github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// TestCondenseSession_CommittedCheckpointCarriesSubagentTokens pins the
// checkpoint-scoped subagent total onto the committed checkpoint's metadata.
//
// Condensation recomputes token usage from the transcript with subagentsDir="",
// which by contract leaves SubagentTokens nil, and that recomputed value overwrote
// the checkpoint-scoped total SaveStep had already rescoped into
// state.CheckpointTokenUsage. Result: committed checkpoints reported
// "subagent_tokens": null even for sessions that ran many subagents (0 of 30
// sampled real checkpoints carried one).
func TestCondenseSession_CommittedCheckpointCarriesSubagentTokens(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	ctx := context.Background()
	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "2026-08-10-condense-subagent-tokens"

	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))

	// The assistant line carries real usage, so the transcript recompute fires and
	// produces main-agent tokens with no SubagentTokens — the overwrite this test
	// guards against.
	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"delegate to a subagent"}}
{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a1","message":{"id":"m1","usage":{"input_tokens":300,"output_tokens":150}}}
`
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName), []byte(transcript), 0o644))
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "test.txt"), []byte("agent-modified"), 0o644))

	require.NoError(t, s.SaveStep(ctx, StepContext{
		SessionID:      sessionID,
		MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
		MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
		ModifiedFiles:  []string{"test.txt"},
		CommitMessage:  "checkpoint 1",
		AuthorName:     "Test",
		AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
		AgentType:      agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
		TokenUsage: &agent.TokenUsage{
			InputTokens: 100, OutputTokens: 50, APICallCount: 1,
			SubagentTokens: &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 500, OutputTokens: 250, APICallCount: 5},
		},
	}))

	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens,
		"precondition: SaveStep records the checkpoint-scoped subagent total")

	checkpointID := id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd3344")
	result, err := s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, checkpointID, state, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.False(t, result.Skipped, "condensation must not skip when files are touched")

	summary := readCheckpointSummary(t, repo, checkpointID)
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage, "committed checkpoint must carry token usage")
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens,
		"committed checkpoint must carry the checkpoint-scoped subagent total")
	require.Equal(t, 500, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 250, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 5, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.APICallCount)

	// The session-wide cumulative must be untouched by the fill, so
	// resetCheckpointWindow still snapshots the right baseline for the next window.
	stateAfter, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NotNil(t, stateAfter.SubagentTokensBaseline,
		"condensation must still snapshot the cumulative subagent baseline")
	require.Equal(t, 500, stateAfter.SubagentTokensBaseline.InputTokens)
}

// TestCondenseSession_SubagentTokensStayScopedToCheckpointWindow covers the second
// checkpoint of a session: the committed value must be that window's delta, not the
// session-wide cumulative, so summing checkpoints does not over-count.
func TestCondenseSession_SubagentTokensStayScopedToCheckpointWindow(t *testing.T) {
	dir := setupGitRepo(t)
	t.Chdir(dir)

	repo, err := git.PlainOpen(dir)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	ctx := context.Background()
	s := &ManualCommitStrategy{}
	sessionID := "2026-08-10-condense-subagent-window"

	metadataDir := ".entire/metadata/" + sessionID
	metadataDirAbs := filepath.Join(dir, metadataDir)
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(metadataDirAbs, 0o755))
	transcript := `{"type":"human","message":{"content":"delegate again"}}
{"type":"assistant","uuid":"a1","message":{"id":"m1","usage":{"input_tokens":300,"output_tokens":150}}}
`
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(metadataDirAbs, paths.TranscriptFileName), []byte(transcript), 0o644))

	saveStep := func(commitMsg, content string, subagent *agent.TokenUsage) {
		require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "test.txt"), []byte(content), 0o644))
		require.NoError(t, s.SaveStep(ctx, StepContext{
			SessionID:      sessionID,
			MetadataDir:    metadataDir,
			MetadataDirAbs: metadataDirAbs,
			ModifiedFiles:  []string{"test.txt"},
			CommitMessage:  commitMsg,
			AuthorName:     "Test",
			AuthorEmail:    "test@test.com",
			AgentType:      agent.AgentTypeClaudeCode,
			TokenUsage: &agent.TokenUsage{
				InputTokens: 100, OutputTokens: 50, APICallCount: 1,
				SubagentTokens: subagent,
			},
		}))
	}

	// Checkpoint 1: subagent cumulative 500/250.
	saveStep("checkpoint 1", "v2", &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 500, OutputTokens: 250, APICallCount: 5})
	state, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	_, err = s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd5566"), state, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	// Checkpoint 2: the subagent grew to 620/310 cumulative — a 120/60 delta.
	saveStep("checkpoint 2", "v3", &agent.TokenUsage{InputTokens: 620, OutputTokens: 310, APICallCount: 6})
	state2, err := s.loadSessionState(ctx, sessionID)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	secondID := id.MustCheckpointID("aabbccdd7788")
	_, err = s.CondenseSession(ctx, repo, secondID, state2, nil)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	summary := readCheckpointSummary(t, repo, secondID)
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage)
	require.NotNil(t, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens)
	require.Equal(t, 120, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.InputTokens,
		"second checkpoint must carry its window's delta, not the session cumulative")
	require.Equal(t, 60, summary.TokenUsage.SubagentTokens.OutputTokens)
}

// readCheckpointSummary reads a committed checkpoint's root CheckpointSummary off
// the metadata branch.
func readCheckpointSummary(t *testing.T, repo *git.Repository, checkpointID id.CheckpointID) checkpoint.CheckpointSummary {
	t.Helper()

	ref, err := repo.Reference(plumbing.NewBranchReferenceName(paths.MetadataBranchName), true)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	commit, err := repo.CommitObject(ref.Hash())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	tree, err := commit.Tree()
	require.NoError(t, err)
	checkpointTree, err := tree.Tree(checkpointID.Path())
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rootMeta, err := checkpointTree.File(paths.MetadataFileName)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	rootBytes, err := rootMeta.Contents()
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var summary checkpoint.CheckpointSummary
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal([]byte(rootBytes), &summary))
	return summary
}

git push -q -u origin soph/fix-condensation-subagent-tokens 2>&1 | tail -2; gh pr create --title "fix(checkpoint): carry subagent tokens through to committed checkpoints" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Committed checkpoints reported `"subagent_tokens": null` even for sessions that ran many subagents — **0 of 30** sampled real checkpoints in this repo carried one, despite logs showing dozens of subagent completions in those same sessions. Two independent drops:

**1. Condensation.** `extractSessionData` recomputes token usage from the transcript with `subagentsDir=""`, which by contract leaves `SubagentTokens` nil, and that recomputed value replaced what `SaveStep` produced. The session-wide cumulative survived on `state.TokenUsage` (so `entire status` still showed subagent usage), but the value written to checkpoint metadata lost it. This is what the two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` markers were pointing at.

**2. The store's aggregation.** `aggregateTokenUsage`, which sums a checkpoint's sessions into the root `metadata.json`, copied only the five scalar fields. So even once per-session metadata carried `SubagentTokens`, the root total was still null. (The `cli` package's own `addCheckpointTokenUsage` already recursed — this one never did.)

## Fix

**Condensation** — fill from `state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens` rather than re-reading subagent transcripts:

- `SaveStep` already rescoped that value to this window (cumulative minus `SubagentTokensBaseline`), so checkpoints stay summable instead of each re-reporting the session total.
- A re-read would return a cumulative snapshot needing the same rescoping, and finds nothing once the agent has cleaned the transcripts up.
- The fill **copies rather than mutates**: `state.TokenUsage` can alias that struct after `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` adopts it (Copilot CLI), and mutating would overwrite the session cumulative with a window delta, making `resetCheckpointWindow` snapshot a too-small baseline for the next window.
- It runs **after** `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage`, which must see the recomputed usage without the fill.

**Store** — recurse into `SubagentTokens`. Summing is correct at that level: it aggregates across the *sessions* of one checkpoint and each session's value is already checkpoint-scoped. The replace-don't-add rule applies to accumulating steps *within* a session, where each step re-reports a cumulative snapshot.

Both `//TODO` markers are replaced with the actual reason the recompute passes `""`.

**Known gap, now documented in code + CLAUDE.md:** a mid-turn commit that condenses before any `SaveStep` in the window has no `CheckpointTokenUsage` to draw on and still records no subagent tokens.

## Tests

All three **verified RED** before the fix:

- `TestCondenseSession_CommittedCheckpointCarriesSubagentTokens` — drives a real `SaveStep` → `CondenseSession`, reads the root `CheckpointSummary` off the metadata branch, and asserts the subagent total is there; also asserts the session-wide cumulative survives untouched (the aliasing guard).
- `TestCondenseSession_SubagentTokensStayScopedToCheckpointWindow` — second checkpoint of a session (through the real `CondenseSessionByID` reset path) must carry its window's 120/60 delta, not the 620/310 cumulative, so summing checkpoints does not over-count.
- `TestAggregateTokenUsage_SumsSubagentTokens` — store-level: single session, two sessions summed, one-sided, no-subagents-stays-nil, both-nil.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

All three PRs are open, each independent off `main`:

| PR | Bug | RED→GREEN evidence |
|---|---|---|
| [#1935](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1935) | Claude Code subagent transcripts resolved at the pre-2.1 path, so they were never captured | Integration test asserting `tasks/<id>/agent-<id>.jsonl` in the shadow tree — failed before, passes after |

Each ran `mise run check` (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary) green before commit.

Two things worth flagging from the work:

**#1938 turned out to be two bugs, not one.** Fixing condensation got subagent tokens into the *per-session* metadata but the root `metadata.json` was still null — the store's `aggregateTokenUsage` copies five scalar fields and silently drops the nested `SubagentTokens`. The `cli` package's equivalent helper already recursed, so the two had quietly diverged. Both layers are fixed in that PR.

**#1938 has a gap I did not close:** a mid-turn commit that condenses before any `SaveStep` in that window has no `CheckpointTokenUsage` to draw from, so it still records no subagent tokens. Closing it means re-deriving the subagents directory inside the `strategy` package, but the path convention lives in `cli` (which `strategy` can't import) — so it needs the convention moved into `agent` first. That's a refactor, not a fix, so I documented it in code and CLAUDE.md instead of smuggling it in.

Next per your plan would be the data-model and integration items (codex `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop`, subagent records in committed checkpoints, Vogon canary coverage). Say the word and I'll start on whichever you want first.

content.text: Definitive answer: **no.** The subagent transcript lands on the shadow branch only, and after the commit it exists nowhere — the shadow branch is deleted at condensation and the committed checkpoint never had it. My PR description overstated it. Fixing that now:

input.command:
gh pr edit 1935 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

`handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` resolved the subagent transcript as a **sibling** of the main transcript:

```
<transcriptDir>/agent-<agentID>.jsonl
```

Claude Code (verified on 2.1.221) nests them one level deeper:

```
<transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<agentID>.jsonl
<transcriptDir>/<sessionID>/subagents/agent-<agentID>.meta.json   # agentType, description, toolUseId, spawnDepth
```

So the resolved path never existed and `SubagentTranscriptPath` was always empty in production. Evidence: across three enabled repos, **every** real `"subagent completed"` log line carries `agent_id` but never the `subagent_transcript` attribute — that attribute is only appended when the path resolves.

Two consequences:

1. The shadow-branch task checkpoint stored **no subagent transcript** — `.entire/metadata/<session>/tasks/<tool-use-id>/` held only `checkpoint.json`.
2. File extraction fell back to scanning the **main** transcript from offset 0, where a subagent's `Write`/`Edit` calls never appear.

The turn-end extractor already used the correct nested path, so a subagent's files were still picked up at Stop. That masked the bug.

## Scope — what this does and does not fix

This restores the capture at `SubagentEnd`, which is **shadow-branch (ephemeral) only**. Verified end to end on this branch:

```
# shadow branch, after post-task
.entire/metadata/<session>/full.jsonl
.entire/metadata/<session>/tasks/toolu_.../agent-<id>.jsonl   <-- restored by this PR
.entire/metadata/<session>/tasks/toolu_.../checkpoint.json

# committed checkpoint, after the user commits
0/content_hash.txt  0/full.jsonl  0/metadata.json  0/prompt.txt  0/transcript.jsonl  metadata.json
```

`extractSessionData` reads only `full.jsonl` + `prompt.txt` out of the shadow tree, so `tasks/` is dropped at condensation and the shadow branch is then deleted — after the commit the subagent transcript is reachable from no ref at all. (Consistent with the wider survey: 0 of 80 primary checkpoint refs in this repo contain a `tasks/` path.)

So what this PR buys today:

- Correct `ModifiedFiles` on the task step — extracted from the subagent's own transcript instead of the main one.
- In-session task checkpoints (`entire checkpoint list`, rewind) actually carry the subagent transcript until the next commit.
- A working resolver, which is a prerequisite for carrying subagent data into committed checkpoints.

Making subagent detail survive a commit is separate follow-up work: it needs condensation to carry `tasks/` into the committed tree (the persistent store already has the layout and an `IsTask` flag, but no production path writes it), and a decision on what the committed record should contain. Not in this PR.

## Fix

- `ResolveAgentTranscriptPath(transcriptDir, sessionID, agentID)` — prefers the nested layout, falls back to the legacy sibling layout so sessions from older agent versions keep working, returns `""` when neither exists (and never resolves an empty `agentID`).
- `SubagentsDir(transcriptDir, sessionID)` — one definition of the nested directory; the turn-end extractor now uses it too instead of inlining the join.

The `meta.json` sidecar is documented but not yet consumed — richer subagent attribution is part of the follow-up above.

## Tests

- `TestResolveAgentTranscriptPath` — nested, legacy, nested-wins-over-legacy, neither-exists, empty-agent-ID.
- `TestSubagentCheckpoints_StoresSubagentTranscript_CurrentLayout` (integration) — asserts the shadow branch contains `tasks/<tool-use-id>/agent-<id>.jsonl` and that it references the subagent's edit. **Verified RED before the fix**, green after.

### Finding 1 — `SubagentsDir`/`ResolveAgentTranscriptPath` landed in package `cli`, which 4 of the 5 sites holding this same literal cannot import

**File:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/transcript.go:112` and `:127`

The diff converted exactly one call site (`lifecycle.go:847`). `filepath.Join(dir, sessionID, "subagents")` still appears verbatim in four other non-test places:

Meanwhile the helper's doc comment ("This is where Claude Code writes them today") reads as a single source of truth that isn't one. The `review/manifest.go` case is the sharpest illustration: `reviewSubagentsDir(st)` is computed locally purely to be passed into `agent.CalculateTokenUsage(...)` two lines later.

### Finding 2 — Claude Code's layout is now a named, documented API in the agent-agnostic layer, applied to every agent

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/transcript.go:108-114`, consumed at `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:847` and `:1149`

`SubagentAwareExtractor` has three implementors, and the dispatcher hands all of them a Claude-shaped path:
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/claudecode/lifecycle.go:25`
- `cmd/entire/cli/agent/factoryaidroid/lifecycle.go:22` (blindly `filepath.Join(subagentsDir, "agent-<id>.jsonl")` at `factoryaidroid/transcript.go:397,454`)

`handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` additionally runs `ResolveAgentTranscriptPath` for Cursor and Copilot CLI, which emit SubagentEnd but don't implement the interface at all — they get Claude-shaped path probes under their own session dirs.

This contradicts `docs/architecture/agent-guide.md:11` ("agents are passive data providers... It only answers questions") and the `GetSessionDir`/`ResolveSessionFile` precedent at `cmd/entire/cli/agent/agent.go:65-78`.

**However:** the interface signature itself already declares this — `agent.go:427` takes `subagentsDir string` and documents it as "specifies where subagent transcripts are stored." Caller-owns-layout is the pre-existing contract, not something this diff invented. **This is acceptable for a focused bug fix; moving it behind the agent interface is a follow-up.** The diff makes the problem *marginally worse only in placement* (it entrenches the knowledge on the wrong side of the import cycle — see Finding 1) and *better in legibility* (one documented resolver instead of a bare literal).

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/transcript.go:112` (nested only) vs `:127` (nested, then legacy)

A third layout change now requires knowing which of the two functions carries the candidate list, and the two can silently disagree per session vintage.

**Deeper alternative:** the root cause is `ExtractAllModifiedFiles(…, subagentsDir string)` accepting exactly one directory, so "current + legacy candidates" is inexpressible. The honest fix is to hand the extractor a resolver, or let the agent resolve internally (Finding 2). Until then, state the asymmetry in `SubagentsDir`'s doc comment so it reads as deliberate rather than an oversight.

### Finding 4 — `AgentTranscriptPath` stays exported with zero remaining external callers

**File:** `cmd/entire/cli/transcript.go:104`

After this diff its only callers are `transcript.go:132`/`:133` and its own test. The "prefer `ResolveAgentTranscriptPath`" warning is comment-only.

**Maintenance cost:** the wrong-by-default builder remains exactly as discoverable as the safe one. **Deeper alternative:** unexport it (`agentTranscriptPath`), or inline the `fmt.Sprintf` into the resolver, so `ResolveAgentTranscriptPath` is the only public entry point. One-line change, zero external breakage.</result>

### 1. Newly activated read + full redaction of the subagent transcript on every SubagentStop (intended cost, but measure it)
- **File/line:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1149` (consumed at `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/persistent.go:550` and `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/ephemeral.go:444`)
- **Concrete waste:** Before the fix, `subagentTranscriptPath` was `""` for every modern Claude Code session, so the store's `os.ReadFile` + `redact.JSONLBytes` branch was dead code. It is now live on every subagent completion. I benchmarked the repo's own redaction bench: `BenchmarkRedactJSONLBytes/Fixture/ClaudeFull2` runs at **4.07 MB/s, 287 ms for a 1.17 MB transcript** (M4 Max, 48 MB allocated, 447k allocs). `redact.JSONLBytes` also makes two full copies of the content (`string(b)` in, `[]byte(redacted)` out). Unlike the main transcript, the subagent blob has **no chunking and no size cap**. Additionally the same file is now read and JSON-parsed **twice** in one hook process: once by `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` (lifecycle.go:1171) and again by the store's `os.ReadFile`.
- **Honest net:** this partly *pays for itself* — extraction now scans the small subagent transcript instead of the whole main transcript from offset 0. I measured full-transcript parse at **231 MB/s** (5 ms/MB), so the extraction saving is ~5 ms/MB of main transcript while the redaction add is ~250 ms/MB of subagent transcript. Net is a modest regression dominated by redaction throughput.
- **Cheaper alternative:** none that preserves the fix's intent — you cannot store the transcript without redacting it. Worth doing anyway: (a) add a size guard so a pathological multi-MB subagent transcript can't add seconds to the hook (mirroring the main transcript's cap), and (b) if you want the duplicate read/parse gone, thread the already-read bytes through `TaskStepContext` instead of a path. I verified this is **once per subagent**, not per checkpoint: the incremental path (`/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/hooks_claudecode_posttodo.go:120`) sets neither `SubagentTranscriptPath` nor `AgentID`, so there is no O(n²) re-redaction of a growing transcript.

### 2. Nit: both candidates are built eagerly, so the legacy path is constructed even when the nested one hits
- **File/line:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/transcript.go:131-134`
- **Concrete waste:** The slice itself is **not** a heap allocation — escape analysis confirms `transcript.go:131:24: []string{...} does not escape`, and `SubagentsDir`/`fileExists` both inline. But the second element runs a `fmt.Sprintf` (which boxes `agentID` to the heap: `transcript.go:105:68: agentID escapes to heap`) plus a `filepath.Join` unconditionally, and it is discarded in the common modern-layout case. Cost is nanoseconds, once per subagent completion.
- **Cheaper alternative:** check the nested path and return early, then build the legacy path only on miss; and `"agent-" + agentID + ".jsonl"` instead of `fmt.Sprintf` avoids the interface boxing and format parse. Purely cosmetic at this call frequency — mention it only if you're already touching the function.

### 3. Test helper does a full recursive tree walk with a blob fetch per file, duplicating a cheaper existing helper
- **File/line:** `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/subagent_transcript_layout_test.go:141-179`
- **Concrete waste:** `shadowTree.Files().ForEach` calls `GetBlob(...)` for **every** file in the shadow tree (go-git v6 `FileIter.Next`, `plumbing/object/file.go:101`) and never early-exits after the match (no `plumbing.ErrStop`), so it keeps fetching blobs past the hit. It also `git.PlainOpen`s the repo and **never closes it**, retaining dotgit/packfile handles for the test's lifetime — every other helper in the package does `defer repo.Close()`.
- **Cheaper alternative:** the identical helper already exists: `env.ReadFileFromBranch(env.GetShadowBranchName(), path)` at `/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/integration_test/testenv.go:902` — it uses `gitrepo.OpenPath` (also the repo's mandated open path per CLAUDE.md), `defer repo.Close()`, and a direct `tree.File(path)` lookup that fetches exactly one blob. Deleting `readShadowFile` in favour of it removes ~38 lines. Real-world magnitude here is milliseconds (the test tree is small), so this is hygiene plus a free win, not a hot spot.

## Explicitly checked and clean

- **`ResolveAgentTranscriptPath` stat count/ordering:** optimal. Modern layout first means modern sessions pay the **same one** stat the old code paid (just on a path that now exists); legacy sessions pay one extra ENOENT stat, which is free. Two stats is well within the "a stat or two is fine" budget.
- **No new walk/glob/read from the resolution itself.** `filepath.Join` + `os.Stat` only.
- **`handleLifecycleTurnEnd` (lifecycle.go:847):** `SubagentsDir(...)` is byte-identical to the inline `filepath.Join` it replaced, computed exactly once per turn end, inlined by the compiler. Frequency and cost unchanged.
- **Integration tests:** no sleeps anywhere in the new file or in `hooks.go`. Per-test `NewFeatureBranchEnv` is the package norm and is required here — the two tests assert *mutually exclusive* on-disk layouts and both call `t.Parallel()`, so sharing a repo would serialize them for no gain. The hook binary is prebuilt in `TestMain`, so there's no per-test compile. The unused `agent-<id>.meta.json` sidecar write is a ~90-byte fixture-realism cost; not worth changing.

So **every turn end pays a second full `ParseFromBytes` of the entire main transcript** — including sessions that never spawned a subagent, where `ExtractSpawnedAgentIDs` then returns nothing. Measured cost: ~5 ms/MB (231 MB/s), so ~5 ms for a 1 MB transcript and ~90 ms for a 20 MB long session, on every turn end. - Folded the legacy path builder into the resolver as two early returns — it had no callers left, so exporting it kept the wrong-by-default builder as discoverable as the safe one.

**Two findings I deliberately did not apply**, both worth their own PR rather than being smuggled into a bug fix:

1. **New unbounded cost on the hook path.** The subagent transcript read + redaction was dead code before (the path never resolved); it's now live on every subagent completion. The efficiency review benchmarked this repo's own redaction at **~250ms per MB**, and unlike the main transcript this blob has *no chunking and no size cap*. It partly pays for itself (extraction now scans the small subagent transcript instead of the whole main one at ~5ms/MB), but a cap is a behavior decision.
2. **A pre-existing ~5ms/MB waste per turn end**: `ExtractAllModifiedFiles`'s documented `subagentsDir == ""` short-circuit is unreachable from both callers, so every turn end parses the full main transcript twice — ~90ms on a 20MB session. Now a 2-line fix thanks to the `paths` move.

### 1. Is a term of `nestedInvocation` redundant? — Yes: `payload.SessionFile == ""` is inert. Collapse to `sessionID == ""`.

`/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/agent/pi/lifecycle.go:166-168`

Directional check (I ran `extractSessionIDFromPath` over edge inputs):

- `SessionFile == ""` does **not** imply `sessionID == ""` — an explicit `payload.SessionID` survives. So that term alone is not a valid predicate; **keep `sessionID == ""`, not the other one.**
- `sessionID == ""` implies `SessionFile == ""` for every input Pi can produce. The basename fallback means any real path yields a non-empty ID (`/tmp/live.jsonl` → `"live"`, `/tmp/` → `"tmp"`, `/` → `"/"`). The only counterexamples are pathological names the extension cannot emit: `x_.jsonl` → `""`, `.jsonl` → `""`, `_` → `""` (verified by running the function).

**Recommendation: collapse to `sessionID == ""` and delete `nestedInvocation` entirely** — a named function wrapping one `== ""` comparison over a struct it barely reads doesn't earn its name, and after the collapse the predicate is identical to the check `HookNameSessionStart` already does inline. Nothing is lost: explicit `session_id` is still honoured (test 3 stays green — verified). In the pathological-filename case the two-term version actually *falls through to the cache fallback*, i.e. into the exact behaviour the guard exists to distrust, so collapsing is strictly more consistent, not a loosening.

Cost of keeping it: a 2-term predicate + a function + a 21-line comment whose central claim (see #4) exists only to justify the inert term.

### 2. Should all three call sites use the same predicate, and is one pre-switch guard safe? — Yes to the same predicate; yes to one guard, but it must be a positive list, not a blanket check.

A blanket `if sessionID == ""` before the switch is **not safe**. `entire_extension.ts:136-138` fires `session_shutdown` with `{ type: "session_shutdown" }` and nothing else — no `cwd`, no `session_file`, no `session_id`. The safe single-guard form, which I verified passes tests and lint:

```go

// same project-local extension, so it fires these hooks with no session of its
// own; the session-ID cache is one per-repo file, so resolving such a payload
// against it hands the child its parent's ID. See docs/architecture/agent-guide.md.
// session_shutdown is exempt: it carries no session identity at all and must
// still clear the cache.
switch hookName {
case HookNameSessionStart, HookNameBeforeAgentStart, HookNameAgentEnd:
    if sessionID == "" {
        logging.Debug(ctx, "pi: skipping hook for sessionless (nested) Pi invocation",
            slog.String("hook", hookName))
        return nil, nil //nolint:nilnil // no session to track = no lifecycle event
    }
}
```

Side note relevant to the design: this is also why the TypeScript guard is **not** redundant with the Go guard. Because `session_shutdown` must stay exempt, the TS early-return is the only thing preventing a nested child's shutdown from reaching `clearCachedSessionID`. Worth keeping both; the diff already says "Two guards" in the docs.

`lifecycle.go:170-173`. Four lines of declaration to save one line at each of three call sites: net **+1 line** plus a name and a jump for the reader, even at three uses. After #2 it has exactly **one** caller, which makes it unambiguously pure overhead. Inline the two-line `logging.Debug` call.

`lifecycle.go:145-165`.

- the mechanism (nested `pi --no-session` auto-discovers the project-local extension and fires these hooks) — genuinely non-obvious;

That case does not reach the cache: `extractSessionIDFromPath` falls back to the basename, so the ID is non-empty and the guard never consults `SessionFile`. git commit -q -F - <<'EOF'
refactor(pi): collapse the sessionless guard and drop what it made dead

Review of the previous commit found the guard was both duplicated and resting on
a claim that is false.

The predicate was `sessionID == "" && payload.SessionFile == ""`, justified by
"keeps the legitimate fallback — a session file whose name carries no parseable
ID". That case does not reach the cache: extractSessionIDFromPath falls back to
the basename, so any real path yields an ID (verified: "/tmp/live.jsonl" →
"live"). The one input where the terms differ is a degenerate basename like
"/tmp/x_.jsonl", which yields "" *with* a session file present — and there the
two-term predicate reported "not nested" and fell through to the cache, i.e.
into exactly the leak the guard exists to prevent. Collapsing to `sessionID ==
""` is therefore strictly safer, not a loosening.

Restructured to match the existing precedent for this problem, Copilot CLI's
subordinate-session guard: one hoisted check before the switch with a negative
exemption for the hook that must still run, rather than three in-branch copies
with three differently-worded nolint directives. session_shutdown is the
exemption — the extension sends it with no session identity at all, so a blanket
guard would skip clearCachedSessionID and break its existing test.

That guard makes both cache fallbacks unreachable, so they are gone; the cache's
rationale comment claimed a recovery the guard now drops, and the diff itself
had already conceded the recovery never worked (no session file means no
transcript, so the event died downstream regardless of the ID). The cache is now
write-only and the comment plus agent-guide.md say so. Removing it outright is
left as a follow-up: the write/clear pair and its test predate this change, and a
single-slot per-repo identity store is separately unsound for two concurrent Pi
sessions in one worktree.

The extension's early return also disabled the tool_call bash hardening
(GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0) for nested processes — a regression, since a nested Pi is
non-interactive while inheriting the parent's TTY and Entire's git hooks fire
from .git/hooks regardless. It now registers that handler unconditionally and
skips only the lifecycle handlers.

Also: fold the three new tests into one table in lifecycle_test.go, where the
package keeps its ParseHookEvent coverage. The old
TestParseHookEvent_CacheFallbackStillAppliesWithSessionFile was misnamed — its
own comment conceded the cache was never consulted — and is replaced by rows that
pin what actually matters: the degenerate-basename case, an explicit session_id
with no session file, and that a skipped invocation leaves the cached session
untouched. Declare ENTIRE_PI_NESTED as a const next to entireMarker, per the
package's convention for strings shared with the embedded template.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>
EOF

input.command:
cd /Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2
gh pr edit 1936 --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Problem

Pi has no subagent lifecycle events. Subagents come from an extension — see Pi's `subagent/` example — which spawns one nested process per task:

```
pi --mode json -p --no-session      # cwd = the project directory
```

Pi auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/*/index.ts` from that cwd, so **the child loads Entire's own extension** and forwards its lifecycle as if it were the user's session. Running `--no-session` it carries no session identity — and the session-ID cache is a single per-repo slot, so resolving against it handed the child its **parent's** ID.

Probed against the real hook entrypoints:

| Child hook | Before |
| --- | --- |
| `session_start` | errors `no session_id in SessionStart event` |
| `before_agent_start` | **succeeds** — overwrites the parent's `last_prompt` with the subagent's internal `Task: …` text and opens a new `turn_id` mid-flight |
| `agent_end` | fails `transcript file not specified` |

So the checkpoint's title and its turn-scoped transcript/token windows described the subagent instead of the user's request.

## Fix

Two independent guards, so neither has to be perfect:

1. **Extension** — sets `ENTIRE_PI_NESTED` on its process (inherited by any Pi it spawns); when already set, it registers **only** the `tool_call` bash hardening and skips the lifecycle handlers. The hardening stays deliberately: a nested Pi is non-interactive while inheriting the parent's TTY, and Entire's git hooks fire from `.git/hooks` regardless of this extension. The marker is read **only** by the extension — Entire's own hook subprocesses inherit it from the parent, so treating it as a skip signal in Go would disable tracking for everyone.
2. **CLI** — `ParseHookEvent` skips any hook whose payload has no resolvable session ID instead of resolving it against the cache. One hoisted guard before the switch, with `session_shutdown` exempt (it carries no session identity at all and must still clear the cache). This is the same shape as Copilot CLI's existing subordinate-session guard, and it also covers third-party subagent extensions and Pi builds that predate the marker.

### Correction to an earlier version of this description

An earlier revision claimed the guard "keeps the legitimate cache fallback — a session file present, but its name carries no parseable ID". **That was wrong**, and it was the only justification offered for an extra term in the predicate. `extractSessionIDFromPath` falls back to the basename, so any real path yields a non-empty ID (`/tmp/live.jsonl` → `"live"`) and that case never reaches the cache. The single input where the two spellings differ is a degenerate basename like `/tmp/x_.jsonl`, which yields `""` *with* a session file present — and there the two-term predicate reported "not nested" and fell through to the cache, i.e. into exactly the leak being fixed. The predicate is now just `sessionID == ""`, which is strictly safer.

### What the guard made dead

Both cache fallbacks are now unreachable and removed. The cache's rationale comment promised recovery when "`agent_end` may fire after Pi has torn down its session manager", which the guard drops — and that recovery never worked anyway: no session file means no transcript, so `captureTranscript` returns `""` and the event died downstream regardless of the ID.

The cache is therefore **write-only** now (written at `session_start`/`before_agent_start`, cleared at `session_shutdown`, read only by tests). The code comment and `agent-guide.md` say so. Removing it outright is left as a **follow-up**, together with the separate problem that a single-slot per-repo identity store cannot represent two concurrent Pi sessions in one worktree — which CLAUDE.md explicitly supports. Nesting was just its most reproducible failure.

## Tests

- `TestParseHookEvent_SessionlessPayloadIsSkipped` — one table in `lifecycle_test.go` (where the package keeps its `ParseHookEvent` coverage): the three sessionless hooks emit no event and leave the cached session untouched; a degenerate `session_file` basename is also skipped; an explicit `session_id` with no session file is still honoured. **Verified RED** against `main`: `emitted TurnStart for session "parent-id"`.
- The pre-existing `TestParseHookEvent_SessionShutdown_ClearsCache` covers the exemption.
- `TestInstallHooks` asserts the installed extension carries the guard.

Also verified end to end against the real binary: after the nested lifecycle, the parent session's `last_prompt` and `turn_id` are unchanged and no second session appears.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF
)" && echo "PR 1936 body corrected"

The exemption matters: `session_shutdown` carries no session identity at all, so a blanket guard would have skipped cache cleanup and broken its existing test.

Recursion depth: real data is depth 1 (`transcript.go:429` builds a flat `subagentUsage` with no nesting), so per-call cost is trivial:

| pre-diff (scalars only) | 172 ns | 48 B | 1 |

## Problem

Committed checkpoints reported `"subagent_tokens": null` even for sessions that ran many subagents — **0 of 30** sampled real checkpoints in this repo carried one, despite logs showing dozens of subagent completions in those same sessions. Two independent drops:

**1. Condensation.** `extractSessionData` recomputes token usage from the transcript with `subagentsDir=""`, which by contract leaves `SubagentTokens` nil, and that recomputed value replaced what `SaveStep` produced. The session-wide cumulative survived on `state.TokenUsage` (so `entire status` still showed subagent usage), but the value written to checkpoint metadata lost it. This is what the two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` markers were pointing at.

**2. The store's aggregation.** The function that sums a checkpoint's sessions into the root `metadata.json` copied only the five scalar fields, so even once per-session metadata carried `SubagentTokens`, the root total was still null.

## Fix

**Condensation** — refill from `state.CheckpointTokenUsage.SubagentTokens` rather than re-reading subagent transcripts:

- `SaveStep` already rescoped that value to this window, so checkpoints stay summable instead of each re-reporting the session total.
- Re-reading was measured at **~29x** the cost of the current call (81–87ms vs 2.9ms on a 6.9MB transcript with 16 subagents), enough to roughly triple post-commit condensation for a subagent-heavy session against the 30–50ms/session budget in `commit-hook-perf-analysis.md`. It would also find nothing once the agent has cleaned the transcripts up.
- `withSubagentTokensFrom` copies rather than mutates: `state.TokenUsage` can alias the checkpoint usage after `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` adopts it (Copilot CLI), and mutating would overwrite the cumulative with a window delta, making `resetCheckpointWindow` snapshot a too-small baseline. The same helper now also replaces the identical copy-fill block inside `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage`.
- The fill is the `else` of the whole-value fallback above it — the two are mutually exclusive, since `accumulateTokenUsage` already carries `SubagentTokens`.

**Store** — call the existing `types.AddTokenUsage` instead of a hand-rolled adder. It already sums the scalars, recurses into `SubagentTokens`, is already imported by `persistent.go`, and is already used in production by `agentimport`. The repo had three hand-rolled TokenUsage adders; this removes one rather than adding a fourth.

**Depth cap (new, and required by this change).** Propagating the nested total into the root summary introduced a write-amplification vector that the drop had been masking: token usage is read back from per-session `metadata.json` blobs on the shared checkpoint branch, so chain depth is not trustworthy, and the root summary is re-marshalled with indentation — O(depth²) in output size. A ~10k-deep chain (JSON's own nesting limit) inside a 200KB session blob measured out to a **~700MB root blob**, written and pushed. `AddTokenUsage` now truncates at `MaxSubagentDepth = 16`, matching the existing `reviewTokenMaxDepth` convention. Real chains are depth 1.

Both `//TODO` markers are replaced with the real reason, including the measured cost. The live-path comment previously claimed `subagentsDir=""` for "the same reason" as the shadow path; that was **inverted** — mid-turn the subagent transcripts are still on disk, so the cleanup hazard cannot apply there. It is in fact the one place the gap below could be closed.

**Known gap, documented in code and CLAUDE.md:** a mid-turn commit that condenses before any `SaveStep` in the window has no `CheckpointTokenUsage` to draw on and records no subagent tokens. Closable on the live path by resolving a subagents dir from session state (as `review/manifest.go` does) and rescoping against `SubagentTokensBaseline`.

## Tests

- `TestCondenseSessionByID_CapturesSubagentBaselineViaRealResetPath` — extended with the committed-checkpoint assertions. It already built the exact arrangement needed (two checkpoint windows through the real reset path) and stopped one step short of the payoff, so a second test would have been ~50 duplicated lines around 6 unique ones. Reads the summary through the store's own `Read` rather than walking the metadata branch, so it does not hard-code the sharded layout. **Verified RED**: `committed checkpoint must carry the subagent total`.
- `TestWithSubagentTokensFrom_DoesNotMutateInput` — a direct unit test on the pure function. An earlier revision asserted this through the condensation path; a reviewer disproved those assertions by swapping in a mutate-in-place implementation and watching them still pass, because `applyBackfilledSessionTokenUsage` already returns a copy there. The invariant is now actually enforced.
- `TestAddTokenUsage_TruncatesDeepSubagentChains` / `..._KeepsRealDepthIntact` — pin the cap and that it does not clip real depth-1 chains.

`mise run check` passes (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

All three PRs now have the simplify pass applied, CI green, pushed, with PR bodies and trails updated. (#1939/#1940 are your own unrelated branches, not strays from this work.)

| PR | Simplify outcome |
|---|---|
| [#1935](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1935) | Helper was in the one package the other 9 copies can't import → moved to `paths`, all 10 sites converted |
| [#1936](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1936) | Predicate rested on a false claim → collapsed; matched Copilot's existing guard shape; fixed a regression I'd introduced |
| [#1938](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1938) | Reinvented `types.AddTokenUsage` → deleted mine; found+fixed a 700MB write-amplification vector |

**The reviews caught four things that were actually wrong, not just unpolished:**

1. **#1935** — I "consolidated" a duplicated path into package `cli`, which `strategy`/`review`/`agentimport` cannot import. My helper was the 5th copy on the wrong side of the import graph. Also: my test opened a repo with `git.PlainOpen`, which CLAUDE.md forbids outside `gitrepo`.
2. **#1936** — my predicate's second term was justified by a case that doesn't exist. Two reviewers contradicted each other on it, so I ran the function: the only input where the terms differ is a degenerate basename, and there my version fell through to the cache — into the exact leak it existed to prevent.
3. **#1936** — my extension guard disabled the `GIT_TERMINAL_PROMPT=0` hardening for nested processes, which need it more than the parent.
4. **#1938** — propagating the nested token total introduced a write-amplification vector the old bug had been masking: ~10k-deep chain in a 200KB blob → **~700MB root blob**, written and pushed. Capped at `MaxSubagentDepth = 16`, matching the existing convention.

**One finding was disproved by a reviewer running it:** my #1938 test asserted copy-not-mutate semantics; swapping in a mutate-in-place implementation left it green, because the surrounding code already returns a copy on that path. Replaced with a real unit test on the pure function.

**Deliberately deferred, each noted in code and the PR:** the ~250ms/MB unbounded subagent-transcript redaction now live on the hook path; a pre-existing double transcript parse per turn end (~90ms on a 20MB session); Pi's now write-only session cache, which is entangled with a single-slot store that can't represent two concurrent sessions; and the mid-turn condensation gap. Each is a behavior decision or reaches outside these diffs, so bundling them into bug fixes is exactly what the reviews warned against elsewhere.

One process note: the review agents left probe files in the working tree, one of which broke `go test ./cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/`. I cleaned and verified a clean tree before each commit, so none of it landed.
