Here's the state of all three.

## CI — green except one gate, and it's not a test failure

Identical on all three PRs: **11 checks pass, `Entire Gates` fails.** The gate breakdown:

```
❌ Approvals: failed — No reviewers have approved this trail
✅ Checks:    passed — Required CI checks passed
✅ Findings:  passed — Agent review found no blocking issues
```

So the actual CI is green everywhere. The single failure is the approvals gate — it needs a human reviewer, which I can't satisfy. `reviewDecision` is `REVIEW_REQUIRED` on all three. #1938 is `MERGEABLE`; #1935/#1936 still show `UNKNOWN` (GitHub hadn't finished computing).

## Review comments — two, both already fixed

**Copilot** reviewed all three (`COMMENTED`, non-blocking). #1935 and #1938: zero comments. #1936: one inline comment —

> `TestParseHookEvent_CacheFallbackStillAppliesWithSessionFile` doesn't actually exercise the cache-fallback path: with `session_file:"/tmp/live.jsonl"`, `extractSessionIDFromPath` returns `"live"`, so `ParseHookEvent` never consults the cache. This makes the test name/comment misleading and leaves the fallback behavior unpinned.

That is exactly the finding my simplify pass acted on — independently, and it went further: the same fact is why the whole second predicate term was wrong. The test is deleted and the file it lives in no longer exists on the branch (confirmed). The comment is **stale by timing**: posted 16:00Z, my simplify commit landed ~18:30Z.

## Trails

- **997, 999** — no findings, no discussion threads.
- **998** — one *unresolved* `code_review` thread from `agent:trail-review` at 15:58Z, zero messages. Its title truncates at 100 chars: *"The new `nestedInvocation` guard protects `session_start`, `before_agent_start`, and `agent_end`, but `HookNameSessionSh…"*. The CLI doesn't expose the full body (`trail comment show` prints the same truncated title), so I only have the topic — but it's unambiguous, and my own efficiency reviewer independently found the same gap.
- **No approvals on any of the three** — that's the failing gate.

Findings counts are 0 open everywhere, which is why the Findings gate passes despite that thread.

### On the 998 thread

It's a fair observation and now inert, for two reasons:

1. My simplify pass made the `session_shutdown` exemption **explicit and documented** — it's the one hook the extension sends with no session identity at all, so guarding it would skip `clearCachedSessionID` and break its existing test.
2. More to the point, that same pass removed the cache's only two readers. A nested child clearing the parent's cache file now has **no observable effect**, because nothing reads it. And in the normal case the extension guard means a nested Pi never fires `session_shutdown` at all — only a third-party subagent extension or a pre-marker build could.

Two things I have *not* done, since you asked me to check rather than act: replying to Copilot's stale comment, and replying/resolving the 998 thread. Here's the current state — it changed materially since yesterday.

## All three PRs: CI fully green ✅

| PR | Checks | Entire Gates | Mergeable |
|---|---|---|---|
| [#1935](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1935) | **12/12 SUCCESS** | ✅ passed 09:35:12Z | MERGEABLE / BLOCKED |
| [#1936](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1936) | **12/12 SUCCESS** | ✅ passed 09:35:35Z | MERGEABLE / BLOCKED |
| [#1938](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1938) | **12/12 SUCCESS** | ✅ passed 09:37:35Z | MERGEABLE / BLOCKED |

The `Entire Gates` failure I reported yesterday is **resolved**. Worth flagging how I nearly got this wrong: `gh pr view --json statusCheckRollup` first served me yesterday's run and reported FAILURE. Querying `check-runs` directly showed a *newer* run that succeeded, and only then did the rollup catch up. So the rollup lagged the truth by a couple of minutes.

## All three trails approved

`nodo` approved each one this morning, on exactly your current head commits — and the gate re-ran within one second of each approval:

```
997  approved  e9a9dcbf1  09:35:11Z   → gate ✅ 09:35:12Z
998  approved  d55dfa643  09:35:34Z   → gate ✅ 09:35:35Z
999  approved  80094e503  09:37:35Z   → gate ✅ 09:37:35Z
```

997 and 998 moved to phase `reviewing`. Trail 999 still read `building` with no approvals when I checked minutes earlier — it was approved at 09:37:35Z, mid-investigation, so that reading was simply a couple of minutes early.

Findings: **0 open** on all three. Threads: the one unresolved `session_shutdown` thread on 998 is still open (non-blocking — the Findings gate passes).

## Still BLOCKED — and it's a GitHub review, not the Entire gate

`reviewDecision=REVIEW_REQUIRED` on all three. The only GitHub review on each is Copilot's `COMMENTED`, which doesn't satisfy branch protection. **A trail approval is not a GitHub approving review** — so these need someone to click Approve on GitHub (or the trail approval needs to propagate as one, if that's the intent).

## A real CLI bug I hit while checking this

`entire trail approvals <n>` is **broken for any trail that has approvals**:

```
failed to decode approvals response: json: cannot unmarshal string into
Go struct field TrailApproval.approvals.author of type trail.Author
```

The server sends `"author": "nodo"` — a plain string. But `cmd/entire/cli/api/trail_types.go:143` declares `Author *trail.Author` (an object). The sibling thread types at `trail_thread_types.go:13,21` get it right with `Author string // GitHub login`, so the convention exists and the approval type diverged from it.

This is why 999 appeared to have "No approvals" while 997/998 errored — an empty array decodes fine, a populated one always fails. `TrailApprovalResponse` embeds the same struct, so `entire trail approve` likely also reports a decode error *after* successfully recording the approval. Confirmed against the live payload, not inferred.

Want me to fix that as a fourth PR? It's a one-line type change plus a regression test with the real payload shape — and it's currently hiding approval state from anyone using the CLI.

content.text:
Done — PR **[#1947](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1947)**, trail **1007**.

## The bug

`entire trail approvals` failed on every trail that had an approval. The approvals endpoint sends the author as a plain login string; `TrailApproval` declared it as an object. Both shapes verified against production:

```jsonc
// GET .../trails/gh/{owner}/{repo}/{n}            → OBJECT
"author": {"id": "e45976d7-…", "login": "Soph"}
// GET .../trails/gh/{owner}/{repo}/{n}/approvals  → STRING
"author": "nodo"
```

`TrailThread` and `TrailMessage` already used `Author string // GitHub login`, so the approval type was the lone divergence. Fix is `Author string`; `TrailResource.Author` stays an object because that endpoint genuinely sends one.

**Two things worth calling out beyond the one-line type change:**

1. **The failure hid itself.** An empty array decodes fine, so a trail with *no* approvals printed a healthy `No approvals on trail #N` while an approved trail errored. The CLI could only display approval state when there was none to display — which is exactly how I misread trail 999 as unapproved earlier.

2. **`entire trail approve` was affected and worse.** `TrailApprovalResponse` embeds the same struct, and `submitTrailApproval` decodes it *after* the POST has already succeeded — so approving a trail reported `failed to decode approval response` for an operation that had actually gone through. Anyone hitting that would reasonably assume their approval didn't land and retry.

## Verification

Live, before (binary from `main`) and after, on all three of yesterday's trails:

```
BEFORE  997/998/999: failed to decode approvals response: … of type trail.Author
AFTER   997: approved  nodo  e9a9dcb  2026-08-11T09:35:11Z
        998: approved  nodo  d55dfa6  2026-08-11T09:35:34Z
        999: approved  nodo  80094e5  2026-08-11T09:37:35Z
```

Tests decode the **verbatim production response bodies** for both the GET collection and the POST result, so the wire contract is pinned rather than paraphrased — RED was a compile error against the old type. I also extracted `renderTrailApprovals` so the display path is covered without a live API, since the bug was only reachable through a trail that actually had approvals.

`mise run check` green (fmt, lint, unit + integration + canary).

## Status of all four

| PR | Checks | Blocker |
|---|---|---|
| #1935, #1936, #1938 | 12/12 ✅ incl. Entire Gates | GitHub approving review |
| #1947 (new) | 12/13 — gate ❌ | Needs a trail approval, then a GitHub review |

#1947's only failure is `Approvals: No reviewers have approved this trail` — the same gate the others cleared once `nodo` approved them. Checks and Findings both pass.

The earlier three still sit at `reviewDecision=REVIEW_REQUIRED`: their trail approvals satisfied the Entire gate but **not** GitHub branch protection, which wants an approving review on the PR itself. That's the remaining step on all four, and it needs a human.

Yes — one of my merges caused it, and it's **#1935**, not #1938.

## What failed

Both failing jobs are the same single test, `TestSingleSessionSubagentCommitInTurn/claude-code` (Linux and Windows). Everything else passed — 56/60. The assertion:

```
shadow branches should be cleaned up within 10s after commit,
found: [entire/695dbd1-e3b0c4]
```

## Proof it's #1935

I diffed the lifecycle logs from the failing run against the last successful run on main (the commit immediately before my merges). Same test, same agent:

| | **before** (21:47, passing) | **after** (13:04, failing) |
|---|---|---|
| `subagent completed` | `subagent_transcript = None` | `subagent_transcript = /tmp/…/subagents/agent-ae63b3ba…jsonl` |
| next line | `no file changes detected, skipping task checkpoint` | `created shadow branch and committed task checkpoint` |
| turn-end | `no files modified…skipping` | `no files modified…skipping` ← nothing left to condense the new branch |

That first row is the exact fingerprint of #1935: the subagent transcript now resolves. That's the *only* behavioural difference, and it flips the branch below it.

## Mechanism

The test asks the subagent to create a file **and commit it** mid-turn. Sequence in the failing run:

1. `13:04:00` — the mid-turn commit condenses the session and **deletes** the shadow branch.
2. `13:04:02` — `post-task` fires. `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` extracts modified files, and the skip gate is:
   ```go
   if len(relModifiedFiles) == 0 && len(relNewFiles) == 0 && len(relDeletedFiles) == 0 {
       // skip task checkpoint
   ```
   `relNewFiles`/`relDeletedFiles` come from the worktree and are empty (already committed). `relModifiedFiles` comes from **scanning a transcript**. Pre-#1935 that was the *main* transcript, which never contains the subagent's `Write` — so the list was empty and the whole thing skipped. Post-#1935 it correctly reads the *subagent's* transcript, finds `Write(docs/red.md)`, and the gate no longer skips.
3. So a task checkpoint is created, minting a **new shadow branch after condensation already ran**.
4. `13:04:04` — turn-end sees no file modifications, skips its checkpoint. Nothing ever condenses that branch, so it survives past the 10s window.

So #1935 didn't break the checkpointing logic — it fixed the input, which exposed a latent flaw in the skip gate: it mixes a **historical** signal ("the subagent wrote this file at some point") with **current** worktree state ("these files differ from HEAD"). Once the subagent's work is already committed there is nothing to snapshot, but the transcript still says a file was written.

Also worth noting: **#1935's own CI run was cancelled** (superseded by the #1939 push 90s later), so this landed unobserved and surfaced on #1938's run. #1938 is innocent — it just happened to be the next completed run.

## Fix options

1. **Gate on snapshottable state** — treat transcript-derived files as candidates that must still differ from HEAD. Most faithful to the gate's intent ("If no changes, skip"), and directly kills the orphan.
2. **Don't create an empty checkpoint** — in the task-step write, skip if the resulting tree equals the base commit's tree. Deeper and catches any other route to the same orphan, but touches shared checkpoint-write code.
3. **Clean up at turn-end** — condense/delete a shadow branch that only holds task checkpoints. Treats the symptom.

I'd go with (1), with a regression test at the integration level driving pre-task → mid-turn commit → post-task and asserting no shadow branch survives — that reproduces this without needing a real agent, which is what let it slip past the canary (Vogon fires no subagent hooks).

Want me to open that as a PR? Given main is red, I'd do it as a focused fix rather than folding it into the open #1936/#1947.

The test asks the subagent to write a file **and commit it** mid-turn. That commit condenses the session and deletes the shadow branch. Then `post-task` fires with nothing left to snapshot — but the gate reads modified files from a *transcript*. Pre-#1935 it scanned the main transcript, which never records a subagent's `Write`, so the list came back empty and the checkpoint was skipped **by accident**. Now it reads the subagent's own transcript, finds the `Write`, and creates a task checkpoint — minting a new shadow branch *after* condensation already ran. Turn-end then sees no file modifications and skips, so nothing ever condenses that branch away.

The gate conflated a **historical** signal ("the subagent wrote this at some point") with **current** worktree state ("this differs from HEAD").

## Fix

The right guard already existed: `filterToUncommittedFiles`, already applied on the turn-end path, whose doc says it "prevents re-adding files that an agent committed mid-turn (already condensed by PostCommit)". The subagent path simply never got it. So this removes an asymmetry rather than adding a mechanism — and it fails open, so a git error keeps the list instead of dropping a real checkpoint.

## Two things worth flagging

1. **#1938 is innocent** — it's just the merge whose run completed first. #1935's own run was **cancelled** 90 seconds later by the #1939 push, so it landed unobserved.
2. **The canary structurally cannot catch this.** Vogon fires no subagent hooks, which I'd already flagged as a coverage gap in the earlier review. So the reproduction is at the integration level: it drives pre-task → mid-turn commit → post-task in-process, needs no real agent, and failed RED with the exact CI symptom before the fix. That gap is now closed for this path.

This stopped being a nice-to-have today. This is the original ask, and it's a storage-format decision I shouldn't make unilaterally:

## The headline result

I verified the coverage actually works by reverting #1950's fix and running the canary:

```

## What it took

Firing the hooks alone wasn't enough. Vogon implements no `TranscriptAnalyzer`, so file lists would have come from worktree state only — and the bug that escaped depended entirely on the *transcript-derived* path. So two pieces:

1. Vogon delegates when asked: `pre-task` → work → `post-task` with an agent ID, with the subagent transcript at the layout the framework resolves (`paths.SubagentsDir`) and the writes recorded **only there, never in the main transcript**. That asymmetry is the thing worth modelling — it's exactly what let a wrong path silently fall back to scanning the main transcript.
2. Vogon gains a `TranscriptAnalyzer` so those records are read back the way real agents' are. That's the difference between "the canary calls the hooks" and "the canary can catch #1950".

Also strengthened `TestSubagentCommitFlow` (item 9): it now asserts the subagent's file is attributed to the checkpoint, not just that a file exists and some checkpoint happened.

**A pre-existing failure I did not touch:** roger-roger fails `TestSingleSessionSubagentCommitInTurn` both before and after my change — I checked against a clean tree. `toolUseID` and `agentID` are derived from `len(prompt)` and `len(actions)` rather than a genuinely unique value. Two subagent-delegated prompts in the same session with equal length (or equal action counts) will collide: `CapturePreTaskState`/`LoadPreTaskState` are keyed by `ToolUseID` on disk, and `setupSubagentTranscript` truncates `agent-<agentID>.jsonl` via `os.WriteFile`, so a second task with the same derived `agentID` overwrites the first subagent's transcript file. This breaks the per-task uniqueness invariant that `handleLifecycleSubagentStart`/`handleLifecycleSubagentEnd` rely on and can silently corrupt task-checkpoint attribution in future multi-subagent canary scenarios.

content.text:
Both reviewers caught the same real bug in my code, and it wasn't theoretical.

## PR comments

**#1950** — no comments. **#1947** — no comments. **#1952** — Copilot left two inline comments, and the trail review agent independently filed the first as a Medium finding:

**1. ID collision (real bug).** I derived `toolUseID`/`agentID` from `len(prompt)` and `len(actions)`. A vogon process handles *every* prompt of a session, and the common case is one file per prompt — so two delegated prompts would almost always produce the **same agent ID**. The framework keys pre-task state on the tool-use ID (`pre-task-<id>.json`) and the subagent transcript on the agent ID, so a collision silently overwrites the first task's state and truncates its transcript. That corrupts exactly the attribution this coverage exists to protect, and it would only bite in multi-subagent scenarios — the ones a future test would add. Verified reachable before fixing (`runTurn` is called per prompt line).

Fixed with a per-process counter, which keeps Vogon deterministic where a UUID wouldn't.

**2. Analyzer contract mismatch.** `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` documented that paths come from tool-use entries but collected `files` from *any* line carrying that field. Now filtered on entry type.

Both now have tests that fail against the old code:
```
duplicate agent ID "avogonX" on call 1
files = [a.go b.go], want [a.go] — a non-tool_use entry must not contribute paths
```
Plus offset-scoping, dedup, missing-file cases, and delegation-phrase matching including prompts that must *not* be treated as delegations. Default canary still 60/60 vogon, 4/4 roger-roger. Pushed as `1e375b84f`.

func TestCodexPostToolUse_PopulatesFilesTouched(t *testing.T) {
	t.Parallel()
	env := NewRepoWithCommit(t)

	sessionID := "test-codex-post-tool-use"
	statePath := filepath.Join(env.RepoDir, ".git", "entire-sessions", sessionID+".json")
	require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(statePath), 0o755))

	// Pre-create state with AgentType=Codex. We skip UserPromptSubmit because
	// the hook handler we're exercising doesn't depend on phase or pending
	// attribution — just on the state file existing for RecordFilesTouched.
	initialState := map[string]any{
		"session_id":  sessionID,
		"agent_type":  "Codex",
		"base_commit": env.GetHeadHash(),
		"started_at":  time.Now().Format(time.RFC3339Nano),
		"step_count":  0,
	}
	initialBytes, err := json.Marshal(initialState)
	require.NoError(t, err)
	require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(statePath, initialBytes, 0o600))

	patch := "*** Begin Patch\n" +
		"*** Add File: docs/added.md\n" +
		"+# added\n" +
		"*** Update File: src/changed.go\n" +
		"@@\n" +
		"-old\n" +
		"+new\n" +
		"*** Delete File: tmp/gone.txt\n" +
		"*** End Patch\n"

	runner := NewCodexHookRunner(env.RepoDir, t)
	require.NoError(t, runner.SimulateCodexPostToolUseApplyPatch(sessionID, env.RepoDir, patch))

	afterBytes, err := os.ReadFile(statePath)
	require.NoError(t, err)

	var after map[string]any
	require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(afterBytes, &after))

	rawFiles, ok := after["files_touched"].([]any)
	require.True(t, ok, "files_touched should be present and an array; got %T", after["files_touched"])

	got := make([]string, 0, len(rawFiles))
	for _, v := range rawFiles {
		s, ok := v.(string)
		if !ok {
			t.Fatalf("files_touched entry should be a string; got %T", v)
		}
		got = append(got, s)
	}
	assert.ElementsMatch(t,
		[]string{"docs/added.md", "src/changed.go", "tmp/gone.txt"},
		got,
		"PostToolUse should merge Add/Update/Delete paths into FilesTouched")
}

content.text:
Codex subagent tracking is done: **[#1958](https://github.com/entireio/cli/pull/1958)** (off `main`, not stacked).

## What it took

The hooks were the easy part. The trap was Codex's identity fields, which mean the opposite of what they look like — I verified each against `codex-rs` rather than guessing:

| Codex field | Actually is | Maps to |
|---|---|---|
| `session_id` | *"identity shared by the root thread and all descendant threads"* — the **user's** session | `SessionID` |
| `agent_id` | the **subagent thread's own** id | `SubagentID` + `ToolUseID` |
| `transcript_path` | the **parent's** rollout | `SessionRef` |
| `agent_transcript_path` | the **subagent's own** rollout | `SubagentTranscriptPath` |

Codex sends no `tool_use_id`, so `agent_id` has to double as it — it's the only value correlating a start with its stop, and pre-task state plus the task metadata directory are keyed on `ToolUseID`.

Two things I'd flag as more than mechanical:

**1. Agents can now declare their subagent transcript.** Rather than teach the framework a second layout to guess, `Event.SubagentTranscriptPath` lets the agent name the file, with the Claude Code guess as fallback. A declared-but-missing path *warns* instead of silently substituting — that silent `""` is precisely what hid #1935 for months.

**2. It fixed a second agent for free.** Cursor has parsed `agent_transcript_path` all along and **never forwarded it** — so Cursor was probing Claude Code's nested layout under Cursor's session directory, finding nothing, and storing no subagent transcript. Same bug as #1935, still live. One line plus a test.

Also worth noting: `hooks.json` uses **PascalCase** event keys (per Codex's own fixtures), while `HookEventName` serializes *snake_case* elsewhere in its protocol. Following the serde form would have produced hooks that never fire — that's the kind of thing that looks fine in review and silently does nothing.

The integration test drives the real hook verbs end to end and uses a deliberately flat Codex-style rollout path, so the Claude fallback can't accidentally satisfy it. Verified RED. `mise run check` green (60/60 vogon, 4/4 roger-roger).

**Deliberately not included:** a `SubagentAwareExtractor` for Codex token aggregation. Codex reports usage differently (`usage` only on terminal `turn.completed`; `review_tokens.go` already tails rollouts), so guessing at it here would have been worse than leaving it — it's called out in the PR.

## Queue

| PR | What | State |
|---|---|---|
| #1950 | subagent regression fix | **greens main** — needs approval |
| #1952 | canary subagent coverage | stacked on #1950 |
| #1947 | trail approvals decode | needs approval |

`/simplify → 4 cleanup agents in parallel → apply the fixes`

You are improving the quality of the changed code, not hunting for bugs. Review
it for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude issues, then fix what you
find. Do not look for correctness bugs — that is what `/code-review` is for.

## Phase 0 — Gather the diff

Run `git diff @{upstream}...HEAD` (or `git diff main...HEAD` / `git diff HEAD~1`
if there's no upstream) to get the unified diff under review. If there are
uncommitted changes, or the range diff is empty, also run `git diff HEAD` and
include the working-tree changes in scope — the review often runs before the
commit. If a PR number, branch name, or file path was passed as an argument,
review that target instead. Treat this diff as the review scope.

## Phase 1 — Review (4 cleanup agents in parallel)

Launch **4 independent review agents** via the Agent tool, all in a
single message so they run concurrently. Pass each agent the diff and one of
the four angles below. Each returns its findings with `file`, `line`, a
one-line `summary`, and the concrete cost (what is duplicated, wasted, or
harder to maintain).

### Reuse

Flag new code that re-implements something the codebase
already has — Grep shared/utility modules and files adjacent to the change,
and name the existing helper to call instead.

### Simplification

Flag unnecessary complexity the diff adds: redundant or derivable state,
copy-paste with slight variation, deep nesting, dead code left behind. Name
the simpler form that does the same job.

### Efficiency

Flag wasted work the diff introduces: redundant computation or repeated I/O,
independent operations run sequentially, blocking work added to startup or
hot paths. Also flag long-lived objects built from closures or captured
environments — they keep the entire enclosing scope alive for the object's
lifetime (a memory leak when that scope holds large values); prefer a
class/struct that copies only the fields it needs. Name the cheaper

## 1. The real cost: newly-live subagent-transcript redaction is uncapped, unchunked, and unsanitized

`/Users/soph/Work/entire/devenv/cli_experiments_2/cmd/entire/cli/checkpoint/ephemeral.go:445-446` (and the git-refs twin at `persistent.go:551-553`)

This block was effectively dead for every agent except Claude Code, because `subagentTranscriptPath` always resolved to `""`. Codex declaring `agent_transcript_path` (and `cursor/lifecycle.go:227` forwarding it) makes it live.

Measured end-to-end, real `entire hooks codex subagent-stop` subprocess, trivial repo so the status walk is ~free:

| `agent_transcript_path` | hook wall time |
|---|---|
| `null` (old Codex behaviour) | **0.19s** |
| real 3.3MB Codex rollout | **1.44s** |

So the read + `redact.JSONLBytes` adds **~1.25s to a single hook**. Rollout sizes across 164 real rollouts: median 481KB, p90 2.8MB, max 9.3MB. `redact.JSONLBytes` measured at 645/442/356/219 ms-per-MB for 0.3/0.5/1.0/9.3MB inputs → median ≈ 220ms, p90 ≈ 700ms, 9.3MB ≈ 2.0s.

Three compounding issues:

- **No cap or chunking.** The *main* transcript 30 lines above (`ephemeral.go:411-418`) goes through `agent.ChunkTranscript` (50MB cap, `agent/chunking.go:16`). The subagent transcript is read whole and redacted whole with no guard, so cost scales linearly forever (~220ms/MB → 50MB ≈ 11s).
- **No sanitize-first**, which CLAUDE.md flags as load-bearing for exactly this cost. `SanitizeTranscriptForAgentType` (`persistent.go:1017`) is applied to main transcripts at `persistent.go:1051` and `:1066`, but to the subagent transcript on neither backend. Codex rollouts carry base64 `encrypted_content`: measured up to **20.8% of file bytes** (687KB of base64 in a 3.3MB rollout). On that exact file: `redact.JSONLBytes(raw)` = **1.31s** vs `SanitizePortableTranscript` (27ms, 3.3MB→2.6MB) + `redact.JSONLBytes` = **668ms**. A 48% saving — the hook goes 1.44s → ~0.80s.
- **Cheaper alternative is a one-field change.** `strategy.TaskStepContext.AgentType` is already set at `lifecycle.go:1280` and simply isn't forwarded into `checkpoint.TaskStep` at `manual_commit_git.go:256-270` (`WriteEphemeralTaskOptions` has no agent field). Or skip the plumbing entirely: the same function already calls `agent.DetectAgentTypeFromContent` at `ephemeral.go:413`.

## 2. Guaranteed-futile full parse of the parent rollout, now newly live for Codex

`cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1251`

`parseTranscriptForCheckpointUUID(event.SessionRef)` parses the whole parent transcript into `[]transcript.Line`; `FindCheckpointUUID` then looks for `line.Type == transcript.TypeUser` carrying a matching `tool_result`. Codex rollouts have no `user` lines — measured type histogram of a real rollout: `response_item: 4371, event_msg: 3034, turn_context: 62, compacted: 4, session_meta: 1`. Measured `ParseFromFileAtLine`: 3.3MB → 17.6ms / 2402 `Line` structs; 9.3MB → 45.3ms / 7472 structs, **`userLines = 0` both times**. ## 3. Two new subprocesses per delegated task, each with a full go-git worktree walk

`cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1131` → `CapturePreTaskState` → `getUntrackedFilesForState` (`state.go:494`) → `gitrepo.Status` (`state.go:437`).

Measured on this repo (1408 tracked, 39k worktree files, correctly laid-out `.gitignore`): `gitrepo.Status` = **64-67ms**, repo open 1.4ms. `git status --porcelain` on the same tree = 19ms, so go-git is ~3.5x; in the documented pathological ignore-layout case this same call was 5.25s.

Per delegated subagent task the diff adds, where before there was zero:

- `subagent-start`: ~40ms in a trivial repo, **~105-110ms here** (40ms process start + `git rev-parse` spawn from `paths.WorktreeRoot` (cache is cold in a fresh process) + settings reads + `initHookLogging`/`FindMostRecentSession` + 65ms status walk + one small JSON write). `handleLifecycleSubagentStart` does nothing else — it is as cheap as capturing an untracked baseline can be.
- `subagent-stop`: **~190ms** baseline plus finding 1's redaction. This is inherent rather than gratuitous — the baseline genuinely needs a walk, and `gitrepo.WithStatusCache` buys nothing across process boundaries. `cmd/entire/cli/lifecycle.go:1197-1199` — `ExtractModifiedFilesFromOffset` now scans the subagent's own rollout rather than the parent's. Codex's impl (`codex/transcript.go:126`) streams with `bufio` and normally sees the smaller of the two files. Tens of ms saved; dwarfed by finding 1.

## 7. Integration test and harness — lean, nothing gratuitous

`codex_subagent_test.go` measured at **0.79s** wall (2.26s package including binary build), uses `t.Parallel()`, spawns 2 subprocesses, writes 5 tiny files, and uses `NewFeatureBranchEnv` like its neighbours. The diff is not efficiency-neutral. Findings 4-7 are neutral-to-favourable, and finding 3 is an inherent cost of the feature. refactor(codex): fix the hook-layer damage the review found, and sanitize before redacting

Four review passes on the previous commit. Three findings would have shipped real
damage, and one of my "fixes" was a no-op with a confident comment.

AreHooksInstalled: reverted to the 4-hook check. Requiring the grown set there
answered the wrong question — agent.HookSupport documents it as "is Entire wired up
here at all?", with drift being a separate question. Requiring 6 dropped Codex from
`entire status` and DetectPresence for every repo enabled before this release, and —
worst — made `entire agent remove codex` print "not installed" and return without
uninstalling, leaving a partially-installed repo un-removable through the documented
command.

The right layer was 30 lines away and untouched: trust.go's MissingEntireHooks,
whose doc comment already says it "surfaces drift when the user enabled Codex on an
older release and the install set has since grown". It now covers both new events,
so doctor reports them and points at `entire enable`.

More serious, same file: declaredCodexEvents also still listed five events, and it
feeds HookTrustGaps. Codex refuses to run hooks without a trusted_hash entry (the
e2e harness pre-trusts them for exactly this reason), so after `entire enable` the
two new hooks would sit Untrusted and never fire, while `entire doctor` reported
trust OK and the session-start warning stayed quiet. The feature would have shipped
silently inert. Both events are now declared, so the existing REVIEW NEEDED channel
names them.

UninstallHooks: the two new types were added to the declaration and to the marshal
calls but never parsed or filtered, so marshalHookType took its len==0 branch and
deleted the whole SubagentStart/SubagentStop keys — discarding any hooks the user
had there. They now parse and removeEntireHooks like the other four.

Sanitize before redact on the subagent transcript, in both stores. This block was
dead for every agent (the resolution always failed), and Codex declaring its rollout
makes it live — for the one agent whose transcripts must be sanitized. Measured on a
real 3.3MB rollout: redact-only 1.31s vs sanitize-then-redact 0.67s, because base64
encrypted_content (up to 20% of file bytes) is the pathological input for the entropy
layer, and it is bound to the originating session so storing it is useless anyway.
Also added the blob-size guard the adjacent session-transcript path already has via
chunking: this blob is neither chunked nor capped, and redaction runs ~220ms/MB.

My first attempt at that used agent.DetectAgentTypeFromContent, which only
recognizes Gemini — so it was a silent no-op for Codex. The test caught it. The
agent type is now plumbed through WriteEphemeralTaskOptions from
TaskStepContext.AgentType, which already had it.

Reuse and prose, from the same reviews:
- Dropped 53 lines of duplicate harness; codexHooker already assembles that payload.
- Used env.WriteSessionState instead of hand-built state JSON, which had already
  drifted: "step_count" matches no field (it is tagged checkpoint_count).
- Converted the new tests to the file's testify idiom.
- Cut the two facts that were each restated 6-9 times (~70 lines) down to one
  canonical home apiece: AGENT.md for Codex's identity contract, the
  Event.SubagentTranscriptPath field doc for the declared-path rule.
- Corrected both comments claiming the fallback layout is Claude-Code-only: Factory
  AI Droid shares it, which also means a follow-up must not simply move the resolver
  into claudecode.
- Moved the capability description out of AGENT.md's "Gaps & Limitations", and the
  agent-guide row out of the "Optional Interfaces" table, since it is a field.

Deliberately not done: table-driving codex's six-way installer. Both reviewers
independently called it house style — claudecode unrolls the same five steps with
more per-hook variation — so converting one agent makes the family inconsistent.

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5 (1M context) <noreply@anthropic.com>

content.text:
`/simplify` done on #1958. Three of the findings would have shipped real damage.

## The one that matters most: the feature would have been silently inert

Codex **refuses to run hooks without a `trusted_hash` entry** (the e2e harness pre-trusts them for exactly this reason). `declaredCodexEvents` — which feeds `HookTrustGaps` — still listed only five events, so after `entire enable` my two new hooks would sit Untrusted and **never fire**, while `entire doctor` reported trust OK and the session-start warning stayed quiet. Both events are now declared, so the existing REVIEW NEEDED channel names them.

## Two more that broke things

**`AreHooksInstalled` was the wrong layer.** `agent.HookSupport` documents it as *"is Entire wired up here at all?"*, with drift as a separate question. Requiring 6 hooks dropped Codex from `entire status` and `DetectPresence` for every repo enabled before this release — and made **`entire agent remove codex` refuse to uninstall**, leaving a partially-installed repo un-removable through the documented command. The right check sat 30 lines away, untouched: `MissingEntireHooks`, whose doc comment already describes this exact scenario.

**`UninstallHooks` was destructive.** I'd added the two types to the declaration and the marshal calls but never parsed them, so `marshalHookType` took its `len==0` branch and deleted the whole `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` keys — discarding any hooks the *user* had there.

## A measured latency regression, and a no-op fix caught by its own test

The subagent-transcript write was dead for every agent; Codex declaring its rollout makes it live — for the one agent whose transcripts *must* be sanitized. Measured on a real 3.3MB rollout: **1.31s redact-only vs 0.67s sanitize-then-redact**, because base64 `encrypted_content` (up to 20% of file bytes) is the pathological input for the entropy layer *and* is unreplayable outside its session. Added the blob-size guard the session path already gets via chunking.

My first attempt used `DetectAgentTypeFromContent` — which only recognises **Gemini**, making it a silent no-op for Codex with a confident comment attached. The test caught it; the type is now plumbed from `TaskStepContext.AgentType`, which already had it.

## Quality

Dropped 53 lines of duplicate harness (`codexHooker` already existed); switched to `env.WriteSessionState`, which revealed my hand-built state JSON had `"step_count"` — a key matching **no field** (it's tagged `checkpoint_count`); converted tests to the file's testify idiom; and cut two facts that were each restated 6–9 times (~70 lines) to one canonical home apiece.

Also corrected a claim I'd made twice: the fallback layout isn't Claude-Code-only — **Factory AI Droid shares it**, which means the tempting follow-up (move the resolver into `claudecode`) would silently break droid.

**Skipped:** table-driving the six-way installer. Both reviewers independently called it house style — `claudecode` unrolls the same five steps with *more* per-hook variation — so converting one agent makes the family inconsistent. It belongs in a PR across all six.

Lint clean, 60/60 vogon, 4/4 roger-roger, pushed. Named follow-ups are in the PR: `ToolUseID` → `SubagentCorrelationID`, a Cursor subagent integration test, and moving the shared resolver into `paths` with claudecode + droid declaring.

For Codex, sanitization strips `encrypted_content` blobs that the function's own doc comment says can be up to 20% of file bytes, so a rollout that is oversized pre-sanitize but would fit comfortably after stripping is dropped entirely (checkpoint stored without the subagent transcript) even though the documented rationale ("sanitize-before-redact") argues for measuring against the post-sanitize size. In `UninstallHooks`, `subagentStart` and `subagentStop` are declared but never populated via `parseHookType` (unlike `sessionStart`/`userPromptSubmit`/`stop`/`postToolUse` above) and never passed through `removeEntireHooks`. They stay as nil slices, so `marshalHookType(rawHooks, "SubagentStart", subagentStart)` and the `SubagentStop` call both hit the `len(groups) == 0` branch and unconditionally `delete(rawHooks, hookType)`. ## Three things need your attention

**1. #1952 was orphaned, not merged.** It closed at `05:47:10` — two seconds after #1950 merged. Its base was `soph/fix-subagent-orphan-shadow-branch`, which was deleted on merge, so GitHub closed the stack instead of retargeting. The head branch still exists but the work is **not in main** (`delegatesToSubagent` is absent there). So the canary is blind to subagent hooks again. Fix is a rebase onto main (dropping the now-merged commit) plus reopen or re-file.

**2. #1950 fixed claude-code but main is still red — now on droid.** The claude-code job passes, so #1950 did its job. But from #1950's own merge commit onward, `factoryai-droid` fails two tests, both with **"expected task rewind point within 30s"** — i.e. no task checkpoint created, which is precisely the gate #1950 changed:

```
TestFactoryTaskCheckpointExistsBeforeCommit                    (142s, and on re-run)
TestFactoryCommittedCheckpointExcludesPreExistingUntrackedFiles (153s, and on re-run)
```

Droid passed in the prior run and fails from #1950's merge on, in both the original and the re-run. I'd treat that as my regression until proven otherwise. It's not the obvious mechanism — I checked, and the filter explicitly keeps files absent from HEAD — so it needs real diagnosis rather than a guess.

**3. Trail 1017 has one genuinely new finding** (Medium), and it's correct:

> The size guard checks `len(content)` against `MaxChunkSize` **before** sanitizing. For Codex, sanitization strips `encrypted_content` blobs up to 20% of file bytes, so a rollout oversized pre-sanitize but comfortably under after stripping is dropped entirely — even though the function's own rationale argues for measuring post-sanitize.

That contradicts my own documented reasoning; it should sanitize first, then measure. The other 1017 finding (High, `UninstallHooks`) is **stale** — I verified all four parse/remove calls are present at the pushed head; Cursor filed it against the pre-fix commit.

Also worth noting: `entire trail approvals` printed approver, commit, and timestamp cleanly throughout this check — that's #1947 working in main.

content.text:
Decisive. **#1950 is exonerated** — the difference is timing on droid's side, not my filter.

| | Aug 10 (green) | Aug 12 (red) |
|---|---|---|
| subagent started | 21:47:11 | 09:22:10 |
| subagent completed | 21:47:38 (**+27s**) | 09:22:14 (**+4s**) |
| outcome | `task checkpoint saved` | `no file changes detected, skipping` |

In the green run droid's Worker had 27 seconds to write the file before `SubagentStop` fired, so there was something to snapshot. On Aug 12 `SubagentStop` fired **4 seconds** in — before the Worker's write landed — so the gate correctly found nothing. The file does arrive later: at `09:22:30` a turn-end creates a shadow branch and commits the changes, so the work *is* captured, just as a regular checkpoint rather than a task checkpoint.

Two independent reasons this isn't my change:
- `filterToUncommittedFiles` **cannot** drop these paths. A file absent from HEAD is kept ("file not in HEAD tree, keeping"), and a path that can't be read from the worktree is also kept. A brand-new Worker file hits both branches.
- The log says the gate saw *no* changes at all — meaning `DetectFileChanges` also returned empty, which is upstream of anything I touched.

Note also the repeated `session-start` events interleaved with the subagent (09:22:14, 09:22:16): droid appears to run its Worker as a **separate session**, like pi does. That makes `SubagentStop` fire on the parent before the child's work lands, which is exactly the shape of this failure — and it makes the test inherently timing-sensitive. Its own comments already concede that ("WaitFor can return while droid is still working", "60-120s turns on CI").

So: **main's red is a droid-side timing/behaviour issue, not a regression from the subagent work.** I'd treat it as its own investigation — plausibly droid changed when it fires `SubagentStop`, or its Worker became async.

## What changed

Fixed the Medium finding.** The guard compared *raw* bytes to `MaxChunkSize` before sanitizing, so a Codex rollout oversized only because of `encrypted_content` (~20% of a rollout's bytes) got dropped even though what would actually be stored fits. It now sanitizes first and measures what would be written; the warning logs both sizes so a genuine skip shows how much survived stripping. The finding was right, and it contradicted the rationale I'd written two lines above the check.

**2. New test, verified RED** against the old ordering: `a rollout that fits once encrypted_content is stripped must not be dropped`.

**3. Resolved both findings** with evidence — the Medium as fixed in `209f70dc0`, the High as already fixed in `59af5153a8` (it was filed against the pre-fix commit `bc40d4e152`).

54	// Fix a failure by re-running the install against the repo and committing the
55	// result — do not hand-edit the committed config.
56	func AssertCommittedDogfoodConfigStable(t *testing.T, repoRelPath string, install func(t *testing.T, dir string) (int, error)) {
57		t.Helper()
58	
59		committed := filepath.Join(repoRoot(t), repoRelPath)
60		before, err := os.ReadFile(committed) //nolint:gosec // path derived from the module root
61		if err != nil {
62			t.Fatalf("failed to read committed %s: %v", repoRelPath, err)
63		}
64	
65		dir := t.TempDir()
66		dst := filepath.Join(dir, repoRelPath)
67		if err := os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(dst), 0o750); err != nil {
68			t.Fatal(err)
69		}
70		if err := os.WriteFile(dst, before, 0o600); err != nil { //nolint:gosec // dst is filepath.Join of a t.TempDir() and a test-supplied relative literal
71			t.Fatal(err)
72		}
73	
74		count, err := install(t, dir)
75		if err != nil {
76			t.Fatalf("install against a copy of %s failed: %v", repoRelPath, err)
77		}
78	
79		after, readErr := os.ReadFile(dst) //nolint:gosec // test-controlled path
80		if readErr != nil {
81			t.Fatalf("failed to read %s after install: %v", repoRelPath, readErr)
82		}
83		if count != 0 || string(after) != string(before) {
84			t.Errorf("committed %s is stale: a plain install reported %d hooks and rewrote the file.\n"+
85				"Re-run the install against the repo and commit the result.\n--- committed ---\n%s\n--- install writes ---\n%s",
86				repoRelPath, count, before, after)
87		}
88	}
89	
90	// repoRoot returns the module root, located by walking up from this source
91	// file's own path.
92	//
93	// Deliberately not derived from the working directory: callers live in packages
94	// whose tests t.Chdir into temp repos, so a CWD-relative walk would resolve
95	// somewhere else entirely (and os.Getwd is forbidden here for that reason).
96	func repoRoot(t *testing.T) string {
97		t.Helper()
98	
99		_, thisFile, _, ok := runtime.Caller(0)
100		if !ok {
101			t.Fatal("could not resolve this file's path via runtime.Caller")
102		}
103		dir := filepath.Dir(thisFile)
104		for {
105			if _, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(dir, "go.mod")); err == nil {
106				return dir
107			}
108			parent := filepath.Dir(dir)
109			if parent == dir {
110				t.Fatalf("could not locate go.mod above %s", dir)
111			}
112			dir = parent
113		}
114	}

Done — #1958 is rebased onto main (0 commits behind) and back to `MERGEABLE`.

## What the conflicts were, and how I resolved them

**`codex/hooks.go`** — main's `a9a676e79 refactor(hooks)!: remove local_dev mode` deleted the `localDev` parameter from `InstallHooks` entirely (`InstallHooks(ctx, force bool)`) and now builds every command unconditionally through `agent.WrapProduction*`. My diff had added `localDev` branches for the two new subagent commands, so I deleted those rather than merging them:

```go
subagentStartCmd := agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommandForOS(cmdPrefix+"subagent-start", useWindowsProductionHooks)
subagentStopCmd := agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommandForOS(cmdPrefix+"subagent-stop", useWindowsProductionHooks)
```

**`codex/hooks_test.go`** — main replaced `TestInstallHooks_LocalDev` with `TestInstallHooks_ReplacesLegacyLocalDevHook`, which does no local-dev install at all. My three lines asserting a 6-hook local-dev install belonged to a test that no longer exists in that form, so they're gone. My 4→6 count updates in the other tests auto-merged.

**`agent-guide.md`** — conflicted twice, once per commit, because main added a `SubagentSessionResolver` row to the same table my commit 1 added a row to, and my commit 2 then moved my row out into its own section. Net result keeps main's row in the table plus my "Declaring a subagent transcript" section below it.

## The rebase surfaced a real missing change

Main added `TestCommittedDogfoodHooksIsCurrent`, which asserts this repo's own committed `.codex/hooks.json` matches what `InstallHooks` writes today — it didn't exist at my merge-base, so my branch never updated the dogfood config, and the test failed after resolution. The helper's docs say to re-run the install rather than hand-edit, so I built the branch binary and ran `entire agent add codex` against the repo: it reported `Installed 2 hooks` and added the `SubagentStart`/`SubagentStop` entries. That's now part of commit 1.

That install also reformatted `.entire/settings.json` (key reorder + indentation, unrelated to this PR) — I reverted it.

## Verification

- `mise run fmt && mise run lint` → 0 issues
- `mise run test:ci` → unit + integration + **56 vogon canary tests** + 4 roger-roger tests, all passing. The vogon subagent canary that landed in main via #1964 exercises the shared `SubagentEnd` path this PR modifies, and it's green.
- Clean tree, 3 commits preserved, 22 files / +613 −25.

CI is re-running on the new head; I'm polling it in the background and will report the result. The trail approval is still the only merge blocker — that one needs you.

Solution: Wire both hooks. Codex's identity fields are the opposite of what the names suggest, and getting it backwards would attribute subagent work to a session Entire has never seen: session_id is "the identity shared by the root thread and all descendant threads" — the user's session — so it maps straight to SessionID, while agent_id is the subagent thread's own id. Codex sends no tool_use_id, so agent_id doubles as ToolUseID: it is the only value correlating a start with its stop, and Entire keys pre-task state (pre-task-<id>.json) and the task metadata directory on ToolUseID. SubagentStop carries two transcripts — transcript_path is the parent rollout, agent_transcript_path the subagent's own.
Rather than teach the framework a second layout to guess, Event.SubagentTranscriptPath lets an agent declare where its subagent transcript is; handleLifecycleSubagentEnd prefers it and falls back to the Claude Code layout guess. A declared-but-missing path warns rather than silently substituting, because that disagreement between contract and behaviour is exactly what went unnoticed while the guess quietly returned "" for every non-Claude agent.
That mechanism immediately fixes a second agent: Cursor has parsed agent_transcript_path into its raw struct all along and never forwarded it, so Cursor probed Claude Code's nested layout under Cursor's session directory, found nothing, and stored no subagent transcript — the same failure #1935 fixed for Claude Code. AGENT.md's two stale claims are corrected: hooks need no feature flag as of 0.147, and "No subagent hooks" is no longer true.

Not in scope: a SubagentAwareExtractor for Codex (aggregating subagent tokens from rollouts). ---
name: trail-backend-env-var
description: ENTIRE_TRAILS_BACKEND=entire-api unblocks CLI trail writes; the two backends key the same trail number to different IDs, and body PATCH 503s
metadata:
  type: reference
---

Set `ENTIRE_TRAILS_BACKEND=entire-api` to make `entire trail` writes work from
the CLI. Stefan pointed this out on 2026-08-17. Without it the legacy (default)
backend refuses body edits with a 501: *"an API token cannot resolve this
trail's editor backend, so the write could target the wrong store. Use a
browser session."*

Two things measured on trail #1017 that turn the obvious inference on its head:

- **The two backends key the same trail number to different IDs.** Legacy
  resolved #1017 to UUID `019ff293-ad1d-7141-a6a9-23ba3d218e39`; entire-api
  resolved the *same* number to ULID `01M07MZT99CKKKGR3VCCQYXRGR`. Identical
  title, branch, and body — so it is one logical trail in two stores, not two
  trails. A differing ID alone is therefore **not** evidence you are about to
  write to the wrong record; compare title/branch/body before concluding that.
- **`trail update --body` was 503 on entire-api for every payload size** (200 B
  through 4 KB), while `--title` PATCH, `trail create --body`, `trail show`,
  and `trail delete` all succeeded in the same minute. The body PATCH is sent
  as its own request (`splitTrailUpdate` in `trail_cmd.go` — the server rejects
  body combined with metadata), so it fails in isolation. Don't read that 503
  as a size limit or as transient; retries across ~10 minutes never succeeded.

A failed body PATCH leaves the existing body untouched, so retrying is safe.
To probe write behaviour without risking a real trail's body, create a scratch
trail — but note `trail update` can only target a trail **by branch**, so a
`--no-branch` scratch trail is unpatchable, and creating one with `--branch`
also **creates and pushes that branch to origin**. Clean up both the trail and
the remote branch afterwards.

Related: [[trail-tune-command]], [[no-fluff-in-review-artifacts]]

You're right that it unblocks trail calls — reads, `--title` PATCH, `create`, and `delete` all worked with it. **But `--body` specifically 503s.**

I isolated it rather than guessing:

- Re-writing trail 1017's **unchanged** 3304-byte body → 503, so it isn't my edits.
- `--title` PATCH in the same minute → succeeded.
- Body PATCH travels as its own request (`splitTrailUpdate` — the server rejects body combined with metadata), so it fails alone.
- Sizes 200 B / 1 KB / 2 KB / 3304 B / 4024 B on a throwaway trail → **503 at every size**, so not a payload limit.
- Retries across ~10 minutes, plus one more just now → still 503.

Trail 1017 is untouched and intact (3304 bytes, title correct) — a failed body PATCH writes nothing.

I also checked the assumption behind my earlier caution and it was wrong in an interesting way: the two backends key the **same** trail number to **different** IDs (legacy UUID `019ff293-ad1d-…`, entire-api ULID `01M07MZT…`) with identical title, branch, and body. One logical trail in two stores — so the differing ID alone wasn't the wrong-record signal I read it as. I've saved that plus the 503 finding to memory so I don't re-derive it.

For the probe I created a scratch trail; `trail update` can only target a trail by branch, so a `--no-branch` one is unpatchable, and creating one with `--branch` also **created and pushed** `soph/scratch-body-probe` to origin. ## #1958 has gone `CONFLICTING` again — a competing Codex feature landed on main

My rebase from two days ago is intact and CI-green on `2fe0fbbff`, but main has moved **103 commits** since, including an entire **`soph/codex-session-end`** feature that touches the same files by the same mechanism:

dec49b8c9 fix(codex): surface SessionEnd in the hook trust and drift checks
1d36ecb67 / 53644bede  fix: address review of the codex session-end work
```

Conflicts are now **5 files**, up from 3, and all in the same places my change lives — because SessionEnd does structurally what SubagentStart/Stop does:

| File | Why it collides |
|---|---|
| `codex/hooks.go` | both add hooks to the parse/force/build/sync/marshal lists |
| `codex/hooks_test.go` | both bump the install-count assertions (mine 4→6, theirs 4→5) |
| `codex/lifecycle.go` | both add cases to the `ParseHookEvent` switch |
| `codex/trust.go` | both add events to `declaredCodexEvents` + `MissingEntireHooks` |
| `codex/AGENT.md` | both rewrite the hook table |

The upside: main now has a merged precedent for "add a Codex hook," so the resolution is a matter of following their shape rather than inventing one. It'll also need the dogfood `.codex/hooks.json` regenerated again, since their SessionEnd entry is now in the committed file.

It's now **`Partial Gates`** (was `Entire Gates`), pointing at `partial.to/.../trails/821` rather than `entire.io/.../trails/1017`:

```

⚠️  Findings:   No agent review has run for the current head

Two are infrastructure noise on the gate's side (`Checks` can't read GitHub; `Findings` wants a review on the current head), and **`Up to date` is new** — meaning a rebase isn't just conflict cleanup any more, it's a gate requirement. Note the gate says 192 behind where git says 103; I'd trust git.

Rebase again onto main, resolving against the SessionEnd work — that clears both `CONFLICTING` and the new `Up to date` gate, and I can regenerate the dogfood config in the same pass. Say go and I'll do it; the approval still needs you either way.

- Non-interactive prompt: `codex exec "<prompt>"` or `codex exec --dangerously-bypass-approvals-and-sandbox "<prompt>"`
- Interactive mode: `codex` or `codex "<prompt>"` (starts TUI)

- Model override: `-m <model>` or `--model <model>`
- Full-auto mode: `codex exec --full-auto "<prompt>"` (workspace-write sandbox + auto-approve)
- JSONL output: `codex exec --json "<prompt>"` (events to stdout)
- Relevant env vars: `CODEX_HOME` (config dir override), `OPENAI_API_KEY` (API auth)

## Gaps & Limitations

<<<<<<< HEAD
- **SessionEnd is tightly budgeted:** 1s default, 3s hard cap, process tree killed on expiry. See "SessionEnd's timeout ceiling" above. This is the only Entire hook that cannot assume it will finish.

- **Hook response protocol differs from Claude Code:** Codex uses `systemMessage` (same field name) but also supports `hookSpecificOutput` with `additionalContext` for injecting context into the model. For Entire's purposes, `systemMessage` is sufficient.

### Resolved since the original assessment

- ~~Hooks require feature flag~~ — `CodexHooks` became `Stage::Stable, default_enabled: true` on 2026-04-23 (openai/codex#19012) and the config key was aliased from `codex_hooks` to `hooks` on 2026-05-01 (openai/codex#20522). No flag is needed.

- Hook config structure at `codex-rs/hooks/src/engine/config.rs` in the Codex repository

259: - **SessionEnd must be trusted before it fires:** Codex silently skips hooks with no `trusted_hash` entry in the user's `config.toml`. Existing users have trusted the four older events but not `session_end`, so the hook does nothing until they approve it via `/hooks` inside Codex. `HookTrustGaps` and `MissingEntireHooks` both cover `session_end`, so `entire doctor` and the SessionStart banner say so — without that it would fail silently. The e2e suite pre-trusts hooks by generating the same hashes itself (`e2e/agents/codex_trust.go`), so **an event added to `managedHooks` must also be added to `codexHookEventLabels` there** or it is installed but inert for every e2e run; `TestCodexHookTrustState_CoversEveryInstalledEvent` fails when they drift.
260: - **A pre-SessionEnd install still counts as installed:** `AreHooksInstalled` gates on the core events only, so adding an event does not retroactively drop Codex out of `entire status` and the agent pickers for everyone who enabled it earlier. The stale install is reported as drift by `MissingEntireHooks` instead, with `entire enable` as the fix.
261: - **`reason` carries no information:** always `"other"`, so a session ended by `/clear` is indistinguishable from one ended by quitting.
262: - **Transcript may be null:** In `--ephemeral` mode, `transcript_path` is null. The integration handles this gracefully.
263: - **No hooks fire under `-s read-only`:** verified against 0.147.0 — a `codex exec -s read-only` run produces no hook invocations at all, so no session is tracked. `-s workspace-write` fires the full set.
264: - **Subagent identity fields are inverted from their names:** `SubagentStart` / `SubagentStop` (schemas at `codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/subagent-{start,stop}.command.input.schema.json`) send `session_id` = the identity shared by the root thread *and every descendant*, i.e. the user's session, which maps straight to Entire's SessionID; `agent_id` = the subagent thread's own id. Codex sends no `tool_use_id`, so `agent_id` doubles as Entire's ToolUseID — it is the only value correlating a start with its stop, and Entire keys pre-task state and the task metadata directory on it. Getting this backwards attributes subagent work to a session Entire has never seen.
265: - **`SubagentStop` carries two transcripts:** `transcript_path` is the *parent* rollout, `agent_transcript_path` the subagent's own. Entire forwards the latter as `Event.SubagentTranscriptPath`, so it never guesses a layout for Codex.
266: - **Only thread-spawned subagents fire these hooks:** internal/synthetic ones expose no user-configured lifecycle hooks, so they are invisible to Entire.
267: =======
268: Codex fires `SubagentStart` / `SubagentStop` (`SubagentStart` / `SubagentStop`, schemas at
269:   `codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/subagent-{start,stop}.command.input.schema.json`),
270:   and `multi_agent` is stable/true. Entire wires both. Two identity details are the
271:   opposite of what the names suggest:
272:   - `session_id` is shared by the root thread and all descendants — i.e. the *user's*
273:     session — so it maps straight to Entire's SessionID.
274:   - `agent_id` is the subagent thread's own id. Codex sends no `tool_use_id`, so
275:     `agent_id` doubles as Entire's ToolUseID: it is the only value correlating a
276:     start with its stop, and Entire keys pre-task state and the task metadata
277:     directory on it.
278: 
279:   `SubagentStop` carries two transcripts: `transcript_path` is the *parent* rollout,
280:   `agent_transcript_path` the subagent's own. Entire forwards the latter as
281:   `Event.SubagentTranscriptPath`, so it never guesses a layout for Codex. Only
282:   thread-spawned subagents fire these hooks; internal/synthetic ones expose no
283:   user-configured lifecycle hooks.
284: 
285: ## Gaps & Limitations
286: 
287: - **Hooks are stable as of 0.147** (`codex features list` reports `hooks  stable  true`), so no feature flag is needed. Older builds gated them behind `features.codex_hooks`; the e2e harness still writes `[features] hooks = true`, which is harmless on current builds.
288: - **No SessionEnd hook:** Codex does not fire a hook when a session is completely terminated. The `Stop` hook fires at end-of-turn, not end-of-session. This is similar to some other agents — the framework handles this gracefully.
289: - **PreToolUse is shell-only:** Currently only fires for `Bash` tool (direct shell execution). MCP tools, stdin streaming, and other tool types are not yet hooked. PostToolUse is in review.
290: - **Transcript may be null:** In `--ephemeral` mode, `transcript_path` is null. The integration should handle this gracefully.
291: - **Subagent hooks:** supported and wired — see "Subagent hooks" above.

content.text:
Rebased and pushed — `fed5c9013`, 0 commits behind main, `MERGEABLE` again. CI is polling in the background.

## The resolution was mostly *deletion*, because main generalized the mechanism

The SessionEnd work refactored `hooks.go` into a table (`managedHooks`) where each event is one row carrying event key, verb, timeout, and production wrapper. So my per-hook parse/force/build/sync/marshal edits — the bulk of my diff — became obsolete. My change is now **two rows**:

```go
{event: "SubagentStart", verb: HookNameSubagentStart, timeout: defaultHookTimeoutSec, wrap: agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommandForOS},
{event: "SubagentStop",  verb: HookNameSubagentStop,  timeout: defaultHookTimeoutSec, wrap: agent.WrapProductionSilentHookCommandForOS},
```

Notably that refactor introduced a `core` field with exactly the semantics I argued for in review — `AreHooksInstalled` gates on core events only, so a newer event doesn't retroactively un-enable Codex. My subagent rows are non-core, which preserves that behaviour, and my long explanatory comment in `AreHooksInstalled` is deleted as redundant: main documents it at the field.

Same story in the tests — main's assertions are now `require.Equal(t, len(managedHooks), count)`, so my seven hardcoded `6`s all disappeared. No count left to maintain.

`lifecycle.go` needed real splicing: main replaced `parseSessionStart` with a shared `parseSessionInfoEvent(stdin, eventType)`, and both sides inserted functions at the same point. My two parsers now sit above theirs; the merged switch dispatches all eight verbs.

## Two things the rebase caught that would have shipped broken

**1. The e2e trust list.** Main's AGENT.md flagged that any event added to `managedHooks` must also join `codexHookEventLabels` in `e2e/agents/codex_trust.go`, or Codex skips it as untrusted — installed but inert for the whole e2e suite. `TestCodexHookTrustState_CoversEveryInstalledEvent` failed exactly as advertised. Adding the labels wasn't enough: the generator also has a `codexHookEvents` struct and a `codexEventGroups` switch. I updated all three, and corrected that AGENT.md sentence to name all three — it currently names only the label table, which is what led me to fix one of three and get a red test.

**2. Drift expectations.** Two of main's tests assert what `MissingEntireHooks` reports for a pre-SessionEnd install. Those fixtures hold the four core events, which also predate the subagent hooks, so the truthful drift list is now `["session_end", "subagent_start", "subagent_stop"]`. I briefly went the other way — adding subagent hooks to a fixture to keep the one-element expectation — then reverted it: a repo with subagent hooks but *no* SessionEnd isn't a real upgrade state, since the subagent hooks are the newer of the two. Expectations and comments updated instead of fixtures.

```
Problem: Codex was the one agent named in the original subagent-tracking request with zero subagent tracking, despite shipping first-class hooks for it (SubagentStart/SubagentStop, schemas in codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/) and despite multi_agent being stable/true since 0.147.

Codex's identity fields are the opposite of what the names suggest, and getting it backwards would attribute subagent work to a session Entire has never seen: session_id is "the identity shared by the root thread and all descendant threads" — the user's session — so it maps straight to SessionID, while agent_id is the subagent thread's own id. Codex sends no tool_use_id, so agent_id doubles as ToolUseID: it is the only value correlating a start with its stop, and Entire keys pre-task state (pre-task-<id>.json) and the task metadata directory on ToolUseID. SubagentStop carries two transcripts — transcript_path is the parent rollout, agent_transcript_path the subagent's own.

Rather than teach the framework a second layout to guess, Event.SubagentTranscriptPath lets an agent declare where its subagent transcript is; handleLifecycleSubagentEnd prefers it and falls back to the Claude Code layout guess. A declared-but-missing path warns rather than silently substituting, because that disagreement between contract and behaviour is exactly what went unnoticed while the guess quietly returned "" for every non-Claude agent.

content.text:
Confirmed on all three points. Here's my read.

## It's structural, and worse than "the guard is unreachable"

The unreachability isn't subtle — it's total. `persistent.go:233` gates every task-checkpoint path behind `opts.IsTask && opts.ToolUseID != ""`, and **no producer anywhere sets `IsTask: true`**. Grepping for it outside tests returns only readers (`explain_export.go`, `strategy/common.go`) and internal passthroughs. So `writeTaskCheckpointEntries`, `writeIncrementalTaskCheckpoint`, `writeFinalTaskCheckpoint`, and the mirrored subagent-transcript block at `persistent.go:550` are all dead code on the write side.

The reason is one level up, and it's the real finding: condensation builds exactly **one `WriteOptions` per session** (`manual_commit_condensation.go:398`). Look at what it carries — `Transcript`, `Prompts`, `FilesTouched`, `TokenUsage`, `SkillEvents`, review/investigate fields — and what it doesn't: no `ToolUseID`, no `IsTask`, no per-task payload of any kind. Tasks are written only by the ephemeral store (`ephemeral.go:367`). There is no code path from a shadow-branch `tasks/` subtree to the durable checkpoint. It isn't a bug in a guard; the durable format has no task concept that anything populates.

You're right that it's not this branch's doing, and I'd go further: it was never reachable for *any* agent. My earlier scan across your repos found `tasks/` in 0 of 80 committed checkpoint refs and `subagent_tokens` null in 30 of 30 — so Claude Code, which has had subagent tracking longest, has never landed subagent data in a durable checkpoint either.

## Was it intended?

I don't think so, and the code is the evidence. Someone built a complete task-writing implementation in the persistent store — incremental *and* final variants, tree paths, the mirrored transcript guard. Nobody writes that unless they expect it to run. The mirroring is what made this invisible for so long: read `persistent.go` beside `ephemeral.go` and the durability looks handled on both sides, so no reader had reason to check whether the branch was live.

There is a genuine design question underneath, though, which is probably why it stalled: a task checkpoint is a *mid-turn* artifact keyed on a correlation ID, while condensation is a *per-session, at-commit* operation. Tasks have no natural slot in a per-session record unless you deliberately nest them under it.

## What survives today, and what doesn't

Worth being precise, because it's not a total loss:

- **The numbers survive.** Subagent tokens are folded into the session totals via `SubagentAwareExtractor` / `AddTokenUsage`, so `entire status` and `tokens` accounting aren't lying — that's the part I fixed in #1938.
- **The evidence doesn't.** The transcript, the per-task file list, and the start/stop correlation exist only on a shadow branch, which is local, worktree-scoped, and reset on base-commit migration and cleanup.
- **Therefore nothing remote can ever see subagent work.** Not the pushed v1 branch, not `checkpoint explain --repo` over the cell API, not another machine, not a teammate. Any consumer downstream of a push is structurally blind to it.

That third point is what makes it worth deciding rather than filing. It means "Entire records what the agent did" has an exception nobody can discover from the outside.

## What I'd do

**Not in this PR.** #1958 is green, mergeable, and its scope is "Codex fires the hooks and the ephemeral path stores the transcript" — which it does, with an integration test proving it. Changing the durable format is the storage-model decision I've been flagging as yours, and it deserves its own change with its own review.

When you do want it, I'd reuse rather than invent: have condensation emit task subtrees under the session it belongs to (`<session>/tasks/<correlation-id>/{full.jsonl,metadata.json}`) by calling the existing persistent task writer, and add a `sessions[].tasks` pointer to root `metadata.json` so external readers can find them the way `compact_transcript` works today. Four things that would need care:

content.text:
Yes. Confirmed both ways, and the empirical half is fresh rather than my earlier scan.

## Why it can't be agent-specific

The break is above the agent layer. Condensation constructs a single `WriteOptions` **per session** (`manual_commit_condensation.go:398`), and that struct carries no `ToolUseID` and no `IsTask`. Every durable checkpoint in existence goes through that one call. Nothing an agent does — which hooks it fires, whether it declares its transcript path, what layout it uses — can influence a field the writer never sets. Correspondingly, **no producer anywhere in the codebase sets `IsTask: true`**; every hit outside tests is a reader.

So the entire task-writing implementation in `persistent.go` (incremental, final, and the mirrored transcript guard at :550) is unreachable for all agents equally.

## The measurement, on this repo's current history

`entire/checkpoints/v1` here holds **12,897 commits**. Of the 150 most recent, **0** contain a `tasks/` path anywhere in their tree. A single one of those commits carries 5,378 checkpoints; sampling 80 of them parsed 71 with a clean agent mix:

```
Claude Code: 58
Codex:       10
OpenCode:     2
Pi:           1
with non-null subagent_tokens: 0
```

Claude Code is the important line. It's had subagent support longest, it dominates the sample, and it has produced zero durable subagent records. That rules out "this is a Codex gap" definitively.

## One distinction worth keeping

"Not working for any agent" is exactly right about **durability**. It's not true of the ephemeral/shadow stage, where the agents genuinely differ and where per-agent bugs live — that's what the merged PRs addressed: Claude Code's stale path (#1935), Cursor never forwarding its declared path, Pi's nested invocations hijacking the parent session (#1936), droid's Workers running as detached sessions. Those were real and are fixed. They just deliver subagent data into a store that gets discarded at commit time.

And token *totals* do survive for agents implementing `SubagentAwareExtractor` — Claude Code today, not Codex yet (I left that out of #1958 deliberately, since Codex reports usage only on the terminal `turn.completed`). So the accounting isn't wrong; the evidence behind it is simply absent everywhere.

Net: one decision, not seven. Whatever you choose about the durable format applies to every agent at once — which is the good news in this, since it means no per-agent migration when it's fixed.

Investigated 2026-08-10 with hook-level probes against the real binary plus upstream
sources at `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/codex` and `/Users/soph/Work/entire/research/pi-mono`.

**Claude Code (2.1.221) subagent transcript path is wrong.** `handleLifecycleSubagentEnd`
resolves `AgentTranscriptPath(filepath.Dir(SessionRef), agentID)` → `<slug>/agent-<id>.jsonl`,
but CC now stores it at `<slug>/<session-id>/subagents/agent-<id>.jsonl` (plus a
`agent-<id>.meta.json` carrying `agentType`, `description`, `toolUseId`, `spawnDepth`).
So `SubagentTranscriptPath` is always empty in production — confirmed: every real
`"subagent completed"` log line across three repos lacks the `subagent_transcript` attr,
and shadow `tasks/<id>/` holds only `checkpoint.json`, no subagent transcript. The TurnEnd
extractor (`lifecycle.go` ~line 848) uses the *correct* `<dir>/<sessionID>/subagents` path,
which masks the bug because files get picked up at Stop.

**Committed checkpoints carry zero subagent data.** Condensation (`extractSessionData`)
reads only `full.jsonl` + `prompt.txt` from the shadow tree, so `tasks/<tool-use-id>/`
is dropped. 0 of 80 primary checkpoint refs in the `cli` repo contain `tasks/`; only a
legacy `v2/full` bundle does. `subagent_tokens` is null in every sampled committed
checkpoint (the two `//TODO: why do we not use here subagents dir?` in
`manual_commit_condensation.go` are why). `TaskStepContext` has no `TokenUsage` field at
all, and the persistent store's `IsTask`/`tasks/` write path is never invoked in production.

**Codex 0.147 DOES have subagent hooks now** — `subagent-start`/`subagent-stop` schemas in
`codex-rs/hooks/schema/generated/`; stop payload includes `agent_id`, `agent_type`,
`agent_transcript_path`, `turn_id`. `hooks` and `multi_agent` are both `stable/true`.
`cmd/entire/cli/agent/codex/AGENT.md` claiming "No subagent hooks" and "hooks require
feature flag" is stale.

**Pi subagents hijack the parent session.** Pi has no subagent events; subagents come from
the `subagent/` example extension, which spawns `pi --mode json -p --no-session` with
`cwd` = project dir. That child auto-discovers project-local `.pi/extensions/entire/index.ts`
